title.zh: 卷一百七十八 列傳第六十六 項忠 韓雍 余子俊 朱英 秦紘
title.en: Volume 178 Biographies 66: Xiang Zhong, Han Yong, Yu Zijun, Zhu Ying, Qin Hong
title.raw: 卷一百七十八 列傳第六十六 項忠 韓雍 余子俊 朱英 秦紘 Volume 178 Biographies 66: Xiang Zhong, Han Yong, Yu Zijun, Zhu Ying, Qin Hong

sentences.zh: 項忠韓雍余子俊

translations.literal: Xiang Zhong, Han Yong, Yu Zijun
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhong, Han Yong, and Yu Zijun

sentences.zh: （阮勤）〉

translations.literal: (Ruan Qin)]
translations.idiomatic: (Ruan Qin)]

sentences.zh: 朱英秦纮

translations.literal: Zhu Ying, Qin Hong
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ying and Qin Hong

sentences.zh: 項忠，字藎臣，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xiang Zhong, styled Jinchen, was a man of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhong, whose courtesy name was Jinchen, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and advanced to vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and later promoted to vice-director.

sentences.zh: 從英宗陷於瓦剌，令飼馬，乘間挾二馬南奔。

translations.literal: Following the Yingzong Emperor into captivity among the Oirats, he was ordered to tend horses; seizing an opportunity, he took two horses and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor fell captive to the Oirats, Xiang was put to tending horses; he seized a chance to take two mounts and ride south to escape.

sentences.zh: 馬疲，棄之，徒跣行七晝夜，始達宣府。

translations.literal: The horses grew weary and he abandoned them; barefoot he walked seven days and nights before reaching Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The horses gave out, so he left them behind and walked barefoot for seven days and nights before he reached Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，由郎中遷廣東副使。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign he was transferred from director to vice-commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingtai Emperor he was moved from director to vice-commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 按行高州，諜報賊攜男女數百剽村落。

translations.literal: On an inspection tour of Gaozhou, spies reported that bandits were carrying off several hundred men and women while raiding villages.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Gaozhou, he received intelligence that bandits were dragging off several hundred men and women as they raided villages.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「賊無攜家理，必被掠良民也。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Bandits have no reason to travel with families; these must be good people whom they have seized."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "Bandits would not bring their families along—those people must be civilians they have abducted."

sentences.zh: 」戒諸將毋妄殺。

translations.literal: He warned the generals not to kill indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his commanders not to slaughter people at random.

sentences.zh: 已，訊所俘獲，果然，盡釋之。

translations.literal: Later, when those captured were questioned, it proved true, and he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the prisoners were later questioned, this proved true, and he released them all.

sentences.zh: 從征瀧水瑤有功，增俸一秩。

translations.literal: He took part in the campaign against the Yao of Longshui and was rewarded with an increase of one salary grade for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He served with distinction in the campaign against the Yao of Longshui and received a one-grade increase in salary.

sentences.zh: 天順初，歷陜西按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshun reign he served as surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he served as surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，部民詣闕乞留，詔起復。

translations.literal: When he returned home on account of his mother's mourning, the people of his department went to court to beg that he be kept; an edict recalled him to office.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home to observe mourning for his mother, the people of his jurisdiction petitioned the throne to keep him in office, and an edict recalled him from mourning.

sentences.zh: 時陜西連歲災傷，忠發廩振，且請輕罪納米，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: At that time Shaanxi had suffered disaster year after year; Zhong opened the granaries for relief and also requested that minor offenders be allowed to redeem their penalties with grain, and the people were thereby saved.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi had suffered successive years of disaster; Zhong opened the granaries for relief and secured permission for minor offenders to pay fines in grain, and the people were thereby sustained.

sentences.zh: 七年以大理卿召，民乞留如前，遂改右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as president of the Court of Judicial Review; the people again begged that he remain as before, and he was therefore changed to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned to serve as president of the Court of Judicial Review; the people again petitioned to keep him, so he was instead appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of the region.

sentences.zh: 洮、岷羌叛，忠疏言：「羌誌在劫掠，盡誅則傷仁，遽撫則不威，請聽臣便宜從事。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Tao and Min rebelled; Zhong memorialized: "The Qiang aim only at plunder; to exterminate them all would harm benevolence, yet to pacify them hastily would lack authority. I ask permission to act at my discretion."
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang of Tao and Min rebelled, Zhong memorialized: "The Qiang live to raid; killing them all would be cruel, yet rushing to appease them would show weakness. Please let me act as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 乃發兵據險，揚聲進討，眾盡降。

translations.literal: He then sent troops to hold the passes, proclaimed an advance in force, and the whole host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then deployed troops to hold the strategic passes, proclaimed a full-scale advance, and the rebels all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 西安水泉鹵不可飲，為開龍首渠及皂河，引水入城。

translations.literal: The springs of Xi'an were brackish and undrinkable; he opened the Longshou Canal and the Zao River to bring water into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an's springs were brackish and undrinkable, so he opened the Longshou Canal and the Zao River to bring fresh water into the city.

sentences.zh: 又疏鄭、白二渠，溉涇陽、三原、醴泉、高陵、臨潼五縣田七萬余頃，民祠祀之。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Zheng and Bai canals, irrigating more than seventy thousand qing of fields in the five counties of Jingyang, Sanyuan, Liquan, Gaoling, and Lintong, and the people set up shrines in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the Zheng and Bai canals, irrigating more than seventy thousand qing of farmland across five counties, and the people erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 陜西數苦兵。

translations.literal: Shaanxi had repeatedly suffered from warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi had long suffered from repeated warfare.

sentences.zh: 成化元年上言：「三邊大將遇敵逗留，雖雲才怯，亦由權輕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua he submitted a memorial: "The great generals of the three frontiers linger when they meet the enemy; though it is said their talent is timid, it is also because their authority is slight."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua he memorialized: "The frontier generals hang back when they meet the enemy; though people call them cowardly, their authority is also too weak."

sentences.zh: 士卒畏敵不畏將，是以戰無成功。

translations.literal: The soldiers fear the enemy and do not fear their commanders; therefore battles achieve no success.
translations.idiomatic: The troops fear the enemy more than their own officers, and that is why campaigns fail.

sentences.zh: 宜許以軍法從事。

translations.literal: They should be allowed to act according to military law.
translations.idiomatic: They should be empowered to enforce military law.

sentences.zh: 廟堂舉將才，逾年不聞有一人應詔。

translations.literal: The court has sought generals of talent, yet for more than a year not one man has been heard to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: The court has called for talented generals, yet for more than a year not a single qualified man has come forward.

sentences.zh: 陜西風土強勁，古多名將，豈無其人？

translations.literal: The climate and soil of Shaanxi are hardy; in antiquity many famous generals came from there—can there truly be no such men?
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi breeds hardy men; many famous generals came from there in antiquity—are there really none today?

sentences.zh: 但格於不能答策耳。

translations.literal: They are only barred because they cannot answer the policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: They are only excluded because they cannot pass the policy-essay examination.

sentences.zh: 今天下學校生徒善答策者百不一二，奈何責之武人。

translations.literal: Today among students in schools throughout the realm, not one or two in a hundred are skilled at answering policy questions—how can this be demanded of military men?
translations.idiomatic: Today scarcely one student in a hundred can handle the policy essays—how can we demand that of soldiers?

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言，而所司守故事不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, but the responsible offices clung to precedent and could not adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice, but the responsible offices clung to precedent and would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 毛裏孩寇延綏，詔忠偕彰武伯楊信禦之，無功。

translations.literal: Molihai raided Yan-sui; an edict ordered Zhong together with the Marquis of Zhangwu, Yang Xin, to resist him, without success.
translations.idiomatic: When Molihai raided Yan-sui, Zhong was ordered to join the Marquis of Zhangwu, Yang Xin, in repelling him, but they achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 明年，信議大舉搜河套，敕忠提督軍務。

translations.literal: The next year Xin proposed a major campaign to search the Ordos, and an edict appointed Zhong to supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yang Xin proposed a major sweep of the Ordos, and Zhong was ordered to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 忠方赴延綏，而寇復陷開城，深入靜寧、隆德六州縣，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Zhong had just set out for Yan-sui when the raiders again took Kaicheng and penetrated deep into the six prefectures and counties of Jingning and Longde, plundering heavily before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was on his way to Yan-sui when the raiders again seized Kaicheng and swept deep into six prefectures and counties around Jingning and Longde, looting heavily before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾忠，帝特宥之，搜套師亦不出。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached Zhong, but the emperor specially pardoned him, and the army to search the Ordos also did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached Zhong, but the emperor pardoned him; the Ordos expedition never marched.

sentences.zh: 又明年，召理院事。

translations.literal: The year after that he was summoned to administer the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was recalled to head the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 四年，滿俊反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Man Jun rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Man Jun rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 滿俊者，亦名滿四。

translations.literal: Man Jun was also called Man Si.
translations.idiomatic: Man Jun was also known as Man Si.

sentences.zh: 其祖巴丹，自明初率所部歸附，世以千戶畜牧為雄長。

translations.literal: His grandfather Badan, from the beginning of the Ming led his tribe in submission and for generations, as chiliarchs raising livestock, became dominant chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Badan had submitted with his people at the founding of the dynasty; for generations the family had been chiliarchs and livestock chiefs who dominated the region.

sentences.zh: 仍故俗，無科徭。

translations.literal: They kept their old customs and owed no taxes or corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: They kept their old ways and owed no taxes or corvée.

sentences.zh: 其地在開城縣之固原裏，接邊境。

translations.literal: Their territory lay in Guyuan li of Kaicheng County, adjoining the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands lay in Guyuan district of Kaicheng County, along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俊獷悍，素藏匿奸盜，出邊抄掠。

translations.literal: Jun was fierce and unruly, had long harbored villains and robbers, and crossed the border to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was fierce and unruly, had long sheltered outlaws, and regularly crossed the border to raid.

sentences.zh: 會有獄連俊，有司跡逋至其家，多要求。

translations.literal: It happened that a legal case implicated Jun; officials tracing fugitives reached his home and made many demands.
translations.idiomatic: A legal case implicated Jun; when officials tracing fugitives came to his home, they made excessive demands.

sentences.zh: 俊怒，遂激眾為亂。

translations.literal: Jun grew angry and thus incited the multitude to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jun stirred the people to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 守臣遣俊侄指揮璹往捕。

translations.literal: The defending officials sent Jun's nephew, the commander Sui, to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities sent Jun's nephew, Commander Sui, to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 俊殺其從者，劫璹叛，入據石城。

translations.literal: Jun killed his attendants, seized Sui, rebelled, and entered and held Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jun killed Sui's escort, seized Sui, rose in revolt, and seized the fortress of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 石城，即唐吐番石堡。

translations.literal: Shicheng was the Tang fortress of the Tibetans' Shibao.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng was the Tang-era Tibetan stronghold known as Shibao.

sentences.zh: 城稱險固，非數萬人不能克者也。

translations.literal: The city was said to be perilously strong; not tens of thousands of men could take it.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress was famously impregnable; it could not be taken without tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 山上有城寨，四面峭壁，中鑿五石井以貯水，惟一徑可緣而上。

translations.literal: On the mountain was a fortified camp with cliffs on all four sides; within, five stone wells were cut to store water, and only one path could be climbed.
translations.idiomatic: A fortified camp crowned the mountain, cliffs on every side; five stone wells were cut inside to hold water, and only one narrow path led up.

sentences.zh: 俊自稱招賢王，有眾四千。

translations.literal: Jun styled himself King Who Recruits the Worthy and had a following of four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jun proclaimed himself the King Who Recruits the Worthy and mustered four thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 都指揮邢端等禦之，敗績。

translations.literal: The regional commander Xing Duan and others resisted him and were badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Xing Duan and others marched against him and were routed.

sentences.zh: 不再月，眾至二萬，關中震動。

translations.literal: In less than a month his host reached twenty thousand, and Guanzhong was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month his force swelled to twenty thousand, and all of Guanzhong was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 乃命忠總督軍務，與監督軍務太監劉祥、總兵官都督劉玉帥京營及陜西四鎮兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhong was then ordered to supervise military affairs, and together with the eunuch Liu Xiang, supervisor of military affairs, and the commander-in-chief, the commissioner Liu Yu, he led the capital garrison and the troops of the four garrisons of Shaanxi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was appointed overall commander, and with the eunuch Liu Xiang as military supervisor and Regional Commander Liu Yu as field commander, he led the capital garrison and troops from Shaanxi's four defense commands against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 師未行，而巡撫陳價等先以兵三萬進討，復大敗。

translations.literal: Before the army marched, the grand coordinator Chen Jia and others advanced first with thirty thousand troops and were again heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before the main army marched, Grand Coordinator Chen Jia advanced first with thirty thousand men and was routed again.

sentences.zh: 賊因官軍器甲，勢益張。

translations.literal: The rebels, taking the government troops' weapons and armor, grew still more powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized government arms and armor and grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲益兵。

translations.literal: Court discussion favored increasing the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated sending reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 忠慮京軍脆弱不足恃，且更遣大將撓事權，因上言：「臣等調兵三萬三千余人，足以滅賊。

translations.literal: Zhong feared the capital troops were weak and unreliable, and that sending another great general would interfere with command; he therefore submitted: "We have assembled more than thirty-three thousand troops, enough to destroy the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong feared the capital troops were too weak to rely on and that dispatching another senior commander would muddy the chain of command, so he memorialized: "The more than thirty-three thousand men we have assembled are enough to destroy the rebels."

sentences.zh: 今秋深草寒，若更調他軍，恐往復需時，賊得遠遁。

translations.literal: Now autumn is deep and the grass cold; if other troops are transferred, I fear the back-and-forth will take time and the rebels will escape far away.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn is deep and the grass withered; if we wait for more troops, the rebels will escape before they arrive.

sentences.zh: 且邊兵不能久留，益兵非便。

translations.literal: Moreover frontier troops cannot remain long; increasing the army is not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops cannot stay in the field long; reinforcements would do more harm than good.

sentences.zh: 」大學士彭時、商輅主其議，京軍得毋遣。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries Peng Shi and Shang Lu upheld his proposal, and the capital army was not sent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Peng Shi and Shang Lu backed his plan, and the capital troops were not sent.

sentences.zh: 忠遂與巡撫都御史馬文升分軍七道，抵石城下，與戰，斬獲多。

translations.literal: Zhong then divided his forces with the censor-in-chief and grand coordinator Ma Wensheng into seven columns, reached Shicheng, fought, and killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Grand Coordinator Ma Wensheng then divided their forces into seven columns, reached Shicheng, fought, and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 伏羌伯毛忠乘勝奪其西北山，幾破，忽中流矢死。

translations.literal: The Earl of Fuxiang, Mao Zhong, pressed the advantage and seized their northwest hill; they were nearly broken when suddenly he was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Fuxiang, Mao Zhong, pressed the attack and seized the northwest hill; victory was near when he was struck by a stray arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 玉亦被圍。

translations.literal: Yu was also surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was also surrounded.

sentences.zh: 諸軍欲退，忠斬一千戶以徇。

translations.literal: The armies wished to withdraw; Zhong executed a chiliarch as an example.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wanted to retreat; Zhong executed a chiliarch to enforce discipline.

sentences.zh: 眾力戰，玉得出，乃列圍困之。

translations.literal: The host fought fiercely, Yu was able to get out, and they then formed a siege line to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: The men fought on until Liu Yu broke free, and they then tightened the siege around the fortress.

sentences.zh: 適有星孛於臺鬥，中朝多言「占在秦分，師不利」。

translations.literal: Just then a comet appeared in Tail and Dipper; many at court said, "The omen falls in the Qin region; the army will be unlucky."
translations.idiomatic: A comet then appeared in the Tail and Dipper constellations, and many at court said, "The omen points to the Qin region—the campaign will go ill."

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「李晟討朱泚，熒惑守歲，此何害。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "When Li Sheng campaigned against Zhu Ci, Mars guarded the year star—what harm was there in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong replied, "When Li Sheng campaigned against Zhu Ci, Mars stood in the year star's place—what harm did that do?"

sentences.zh: 」日遣兵薄城下，焚芻草，絕汲道。

translations.literal: Each day he sent troops to press the walls, burned fodder grass, and cut off their water routes.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he sent troops to press the walls, burned the fodder grass, and cut off their water supply.

sentences.zh: 賊窘欲降，邀忠與文升相見。

translations.literal: The rebels, hard pressed, wished to surrender and invited Zhong and Wensheng to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the rebels wished to surrender and asked to meet Zhong and Ma Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 忠偕劉玉單騎赴之，文升亦從數十騎至，呼俊、璹諭以速降。

translations.literal: Zhong went with Liu Yu alone on horseback; Wensheng also came with several dozen horsemen and called to Jun and Sui, urging them to surrender quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong rode out alone with Liu Yu; Ma Wensheng came with a few dozen horsemen and called to Jun and Sui to surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 賊遙望羅拜，忠直前挾璹以歸。

translations.literal: The rebels bowed from afar in ranks; Zhong went straight forward, seized Sui, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bowed from a distance; Zhong rode forward, seized Sui, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 俊氣沮，猶豫不出。

translations.literal: Jun's spirit was crushed, yet he hesitated and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's spirit broke, but he still hesitated to come out.

sentences.zh: 忠命縛木為橋，人負土囊填濠塹，擊以銅炮，死者益眾。

translations.literal: Zhong ordered timbers lashed into bridges; men carried earth bags to fill moats and ditches; they struck with bronze cannon, and the dead grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had timbers lashed into bridges; men carried earth-filled sacks to fill the moats, and bronze cannon fire piled up the dead.

sentences.zh: 賊倚愛將楊虎貍為謀主，夜出汲被擒。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on their beloved general Yang Hulu as strategist; he went out at night to draw water and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels relied on their favorite commander Yang Hulu as strategist; he went out one night to draw water and was captured.

sentences.zh: 忠貰其死，諭以購賊賞格。

translations.literal: Zhong spared his life and instructed him in the bounty offered for capturing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong spared his life and told him the reward scale for turning in rebels.

sentences.zh: 示之金，且賜金帶鉤。

translations.literal: He showed him gold and also bestowed a gold belt hook.
translations.idiomatic: He showed him gold and gave him a gold belt hook as a gift.

sentences.zh: 縱歸，使誘俊出戰，伏兵擒焉。

translations.literal: He released him to return and had him lure Jun out to battle; ambush troops seized him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent him back to lure Jun out to fight; ambush troops seized Jun.

sentences.zh: 急擊下石城，盡獲余寇。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack, took Shicheng, and captured all the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Shicheng and captured all the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 毀其城，鑿石紀功。

translations.literal: They destroyed the city and carved stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: They razed the fortress and carved an inscription in stone to commemorate the victory.

sentences.zh: 增一衛於固原西北西安廢城，留兵戍之而還。

translations.literal: They added one guard at the abandoned city of Xi'an northwest of Guyuan, left troops to garrison it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They established a new guard post at the abandoned city of Xi'an northwest of Guyuan, left a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，石城未下，天甚寒，士卒頗困。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Shicheng fell, the weather was very cold and the soldiers were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shicheng fell, the weather was bitterly cold and the troops were suffering badly.

sentences.zh: 忠慮賊奔突，乘凍渡河與套寇合，日夜治攻具。

translations.literal: Zhong feared the rebels would break out, cross the frozen river while it was hard, and join the Ordos raiders; day and night he prepared siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong feared the rebels would break out, cross the frozen river, and join the Ordos raiders, so he worked day and night preparing siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 身當矢石不少避，大小三百余戰。

translations.literal: He himself faced arrows and stones without shrinking, in more than three hundred engagements great and small.
translations.idiomatic: He personally faced arrows and stones without flinching through more than three hundred engagements, large and small.

sentences.zh: 彭時、商輅知忠能辦賊，不從中制，卒用殄賊。

translations.literal: Peng Shi and Shang Lu knew Zhong could handle the rebels and did not interfere from the center; in the end he was able to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi and Shang Lu knew Zhong could finish the job and did not interfere from the capital; in the end the rebels were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都御史，與林聰協掌院事。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was advanced to right censor-in-chief and joined Lin Cong in jointly administering the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to right censor-in-chief and shared administration of the Censorate with Lin Cong.

sentences.zh: 白圭既平劉通，荊、襄間流民屯結如故。

translations.literal: After Bai Gui had pacified Liu Tong, the displaced people between Jing and Xiang remained gathered in encampments as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Bai Gui suppressed Liu Tong, displaced people between Jing and Xiang still clustered in camps as before.

sentences.zh: 通黨李胡子者名原，偽稱平王，與小王洪、王彪等掠南漳、房、內鄉、渭南諸縣。

translations.literal: Liu Tong's partisan Li Huzi, whose name was Yuan, falsely styled himself the Prince of Peace and, with the lesser kings Hong and Wang Biao and others, raided the counties of Nanzhang, Fang, Neixiang, Weinan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tong's follower Li Huzi, whose given name was Yuan, styled himself the Prince of Peace and, with Hong and Wang Biao and others, raided Nanzhang, Fang, Neixiang, Weinan, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 流民附賊者至百萬。

translations.literal: Displaced people who joined the rebels reached a million.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people who joined the rebels numbered as many as a million.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，詔忠總督軍務，與湖廣總兵官李震討之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year an edict ordered Zhong to supervise military affairs and, with the commander-in-chief of Huguang, Li Zhen, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year Zhong was ordered to take overall command and, with Huguang Commander Li Zhen, suppress them.

sentences.zh: 忠乃奏調永順、保靖土兵。

translations.literal: Zhong then memorialized to transfer the native troops of Yongshun and Baojing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong memorialized to mobilize the native troops of Yongshun and Baojing.

sentences.zh: 而先分軍列要害，多設旗幟鉦鼓，遣人入山招諭。

translations.literal: But first he divided the army to hold key points, set up many banners, gongs, and drums, and sent men into the mountains to summon and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: First he deployed troops at key points, set up banners, gongs, and drums, and sent men into the mountains to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 流民歸者四十余萬，彪亦就擒。

translations.literal: More than four hundred thousand displaced people returned, and Biao was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred thousand displaced people came back, and Wang Biao was captured.

sentences.zh: 時白圭為兵部，遣錦衣百戶吳綬贊參將王信軍。

translations.literal: At that time Bai Gui was at the Ministry of War and sent the hundred-household Wu Shou of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to assist the vice-commander Wang Xin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui was then Minister of War; he sent Embroidered Guard officer Wu Shou to assist Vice-Commander Wang Xin's force.

sentences.zh: 綬欲攘功，不利賊瓦解。

translations.literal: Shou wished to seize the credit and did not want the rebels to disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shou wanted the credit for himself and did not want the rebels to collapse peacefully.

sentences.zh: 縱流言，圭信之，止土兵毋調。

translations.literal: He spread rumors; Gui believed them and halted the transfer of native troops.
translations.idiomatic: He spread rumors; Bai Gui believed them and halted the native troops' mobilization.

sentences.zh: 忠疏爭，且劾綬罪，帝為召綬還，而聽調土兵如故。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized in protest and also impeached Shou for his crimes; the emperor recalled Shou and allowed the native troops to be transferred as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong protested by memorial and impeached Wu Shou; the emperor recalled Shou and allowed the native troops to be mobilized as planned.

sentences.zh: 合二十五萬，分八道逼之，流民歸者又數萬。

translations.literal: Altogether two hundred fifty thousand men were assembled; they pressed in eight columns, and tens of thousands more displaced people returned.
translations.idiomatic: With two hundred fifty thousand men assembled, they pressed in eight columns, and tens of thousands more displaced people returned.

sentences.zh: 賊潛伏山寨，伺間出劫。

translations.literal: The rebels lurked in mountain stockades and watched for openings to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hid in mountain stockades and struck whenever they saw an opening.

sentences.zh: 忠命副使余洵、都指揮李振擊之，遇於竹山。

translations.literal: Zhong ordered the vice-commissioner Yu Xun and the regional commander Li Zhen to attack them and met them at Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong ordered Vice-Commissioner Yu Xun and Regional Commander Li Zhen to attack them and met the rebels at Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 乘溪漲半渡截擊，擒李原、小王洪等，賊多溺死。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the swollen stream, they struck while the rebels were half across; they captured Li Yuan, the lesser king Hong, and others, and many rebels drowned.
translations.idiomatic: They struck while the rebels were half across the swollen stream, capturing Li Yuan and the lesser king Hong; many rebels drowned.

sentences.zh: 忠移軍竹山，捕余孽。

translations.literal: Zhong moved his army to Zhushan to hunt down the remnants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong moved his army to Zhushan to hunt down the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 復招流民五十萬，斬首六百四十，俘八百有奇，家口三萬余人。

translations.literal: He again summoned five hundred thousand displaced people; heads cut numbered six hundred forty, captives more than eight hundred, and dependents more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He brought back another five hundred thousand displaced people, took six hundred forty heads, captured more than eight hundred rebels, and seized more than thirty thousand dependents.

sentences.zh: 戶選一丁，戍湖廣邊衛，余令歸籍給田。

translations.literal: From each household one man was chosen to garrison the frontier guards of Huguang; the rest were ordered to return to their registers and were given fields.
translations.idiomatic: From each household one man was drafted to garrison Huguang's frontier guards; the rest were sent home to their registers and given farmland.

sentences.zh: 疏陳善後十事，悉允行。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth ten measures for follow-up pacification, and all were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized ten follow-up measures for pacification, and the court approved them all.

sentences.zh: 忠之下令逐流民也，有司一切驅逼。

translations.literal: When Zhong ordered the expulsion of displaced people, the local offices drove and pressed them indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong ordered displaced people expelled, local officials drove everyone out without distinction.

sentences.zh: 不前，即殺之。

translations.literal: Those who did not go forward were killed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who lagged behind was killed.

sentences.zh: 民有自洪武中占籍者，亦在遺中。

translations.literal: People who had been registered since the Hongwu reign were also among those cast out.
translations.idiomatic: People who had held registered residence since the Hongwu reign were expelled along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 戍者舟行多疫死。

translations.literal: Many of those sent to garrison duty died of plague while traveling by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Many of those sent to the frontier garrisons died of plague on the boats.

sentences.zh: 給事中梁璟因星變求言，劾忠妄殺。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Liang Jing, citing an irregularity in the stars, requested frank counsel and impeached Zhong for indiscriminate killing.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liang Jing, citing a celestial omen, called for frank counsel and impeached Zhong for indiscriminate killing.

sentences.zh: 白圭亦言流民既成業者，宜隨所在著籍，又駁忠所上功次互異。

translations.literal: Bai Gui also said that displaced people who had already established livelihoods should be registered wherever they were, and he also refuted the inconsistencies in Zhong's submitted roster of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui also argued that displaced people who had already settled should be registered where they were, and he challenged inconsistencies in Zhong's merit reports.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not heed any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected all of these objections.

sentences.zh: 進忠左都御史。

translations.literal: Zhong was advanced to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 蔭子綬錦衣千戶，諸將錄功有差。

translations.literal: His son Jing was ennobled as a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and the generals had their merit recorded with varying rewards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing received an hereditary post as chiliarch in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and the generals were rewarded according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 忠上疏言：「臣先後招撫流民復業者九十三萬余人，賊黨遁入深山，又招諭解散自歸者五十萬人。

translations.literal: Zhong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has successively summoned and settled more than nine hundred thirty thousand displaced people to resume their livelihoods; rebel partisans who fled into deep mountains were again summoned and instructed to disband and return of their own accord—five hundred thousand people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong memorialized: "I have settled more than nine hundred thirty thousand displaced people back into productive life. Another five hundred thousand who had fled into the mountains came back when summoned to disband."

sentences.zh: 俘獲百人，皆首惡耳。

translations.literal: The hundred captives were all ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred prisoners taken were all ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 今言皆良家子，則前此屢奏猖獗難禦者，伊誰也？

translations.literal: Now if it is said they were all good families' sons, then who were those I repeatedly reported as rampant and hard to control?
translations.idiomatic: If they were all innocent commoners, who were the rampant rebels I repeatedly reported as impossible to control?

sentences.zh: 賊黨罪固當死，正因不忍濫誅，故令丁壯謫發遣戍。

translations.literal: The rebel partisans deserved death by law; precisely because I could not bear indiscriminate slaughter, I had able-bodied men banished and sent to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel partisans deserved death, but unwilling to slaughter indiscriminately, I sent able-bodied men to frontier garrison duty instead.

sentences.zh: 其久附籍者，或乃占山四十餘里，招聚無賴千人，爭鬥劫殺。

translations.literal: Among those long registered, some had occupied more than forty li of mountain, gathered more than a thousand ruffians, and fought, robbed, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Some who had long held registered residence had seized more than forty li of mountain land, gathered a thousand ruffians, and fought, robbed, and killed.

sentences.zh: 若此者，可以久居故不遣乎？

translations.literal: Could such men be left undisturbed because they had lived there long?
translations.idiomatic: Were such men to be left alone simply because they had lived there a long time?

sentences.zh: 臣揭榜曉賊，謂已殺數千，蓋張虛勢怵之，非實事也。

translations.literal: When your servant posted proclamations to warn the rebels, saying several thousand had been killed, it was to inflate a false threat and frighten them—not fact.
translations.idiomatic: When I posted proclamations claiming several thousand had been killed, that was bluff to frighten them—not fact.

sentences.zh: 且圭固嘗身任其事，今日之事又圭所遺。

translations.literal: Moreover Gui had personally taken charge of the affair; today's troubles are also what Gui left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Bai Gui had personally handled this affair; today's troubles are the legacy he left behind.

sentences.zh: 先時，中外議者謂荊、襄之患何日得寧。

translations.literal: Earlier, commentators inside and outside the court asked when the troubles of Jing and Xiang would ever be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, court and country alike wondered when the troubles of Jing and Xiang would ever end.

sentences.zh: 今幸平靖，而流言沸騰，以臣為口實。

translations.literal: Now that peace has fortunately been restored, rumors boil over and use your servant as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the region is finally at peace, rumors boil over and make me their target.

sentences.zh: 昔馬援薏苡蒙謗，鄧艾檻車被征。

translations.literal: In the past Ma Yuan was slandered over Job's tears, and Deng Ai was summoned in a prisoner cart.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan was slandered over Job's tears, and Deng Ai was summoned home in a prisoner cart.

sentences.zh: 功不見錄，身更不保。

translations.literal: Their merit went unrecognized and they could not even preserve their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Their merit went unrecognized and they could not even save themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣幸際聖明，願賜骸骨，勿使臣為馬、鄧之續。

translations.literal: Your servant has fortunately encountered a sage reign; I beg to be granted my bones and not made to follow in the steps of Ma and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: I have been fortunate to serve a sage reign; I beg leave to retire and not share the fate of Ma Yuan and Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 」帝溫詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 八年召還，與李賓協掌院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled and joined Li Bin in jointly administering the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled to share administration of the Censorate with Li Bin.

sentences.zh: 後二年拜刑部尚書，尋代圭為兵部。

translations.literal: Two years later he was appointed minister of justice and soon replaced Gui as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became Minister of Justice and soon replaced Bai Gui as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 汪直開西廠，恣橫，忠屢遭侮不能堪。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi opened the Western Depot and acted with reckless arrogance; Zhong was repeatedly insulted and could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi opened the Western Depot and acted with reckless arrogance, Zhong was repeatedly humiliated and could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 會大學士商輅等劾直，忠亦倡九卿劾之。

translations.literal: When the grand secretary Shang Lu and others impeached Zhi, Zhong also led the nine chief ministers in impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Shang Lu and others impeached Wang Zhi, Zhong also led the nine chief ministers in doing so.

sentences.zh: 奏留中，而西廠遂罷，直深恨之。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept at court, yet the Western Depot was abolished; Zhi hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was kept at court, but the Western Depot was abolished; Wang Zhi hated Zhong deeply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，西廠復設，直以吳綬為腹心，綬挾前憾，伺忠益急。

translations.literal: Before long the Western Depot was re-established; Zhi made Wu Shou his trusted confidant, and Shou, nursing his old grudge, watched for chances against Zhong all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Western Depot was restored; Wang Zhi made Wu Shou his right hand, and Shou, nursing his old grudge, watched for chances against Zhong all the more closely.

sentences.zh: 忠不自安，乞歸治病。

translations.literal: Zhong felt insecure and begged to return home to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Zhong asked to retire home to treat his illness.

sentences.zh: 未行，而綬嗾偵事者誣忠罪。

translations.literal: Before he could leave, Shou incited investigators to frame Zhong with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Wu Shou incited investigators to frame Zhong with crimes.

sentences.zh: 給事中郭鏜、御史馮貫等復交章劾忠，事連其子經、太監黃賜、興寧伯李震、彰武伯楊信等。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Guo Yong, the censor Feng Guan, and others again submitted successive memorials impeaching Zhong, implicating his son Jing, the eunuch Huang Ci, the Earl of Xingning Li Zhen, the Marquis of Zhangwu Yang Xin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Guo Yong, Censor Feng Guan, and others impeached Zhong again, implicating his son Jing, the eunuch Huang Ci, the Earl of Xingning Li Zhen, the Marquis of Zhangwu Yang Xin, and others.

sentences.zh: 詔法司會錦衣衛廷鞫，忠抗辯不少屈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the judicial offices together with the Embroidered Uniform Guard to try him at court; Zhong argued in his defense without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a joint trial by the judicial offices and the Embroidered Uniform Guard; Zhong defended himself without yielding.

sentences.zh: 然眾知出直意，無敢為之白者，竟斥為民，賜與震等亦得罪。

translations.literal: Yet everyone knew this came from Zhi's will; none dared speak for him, and in the end he was dismissed to commoner status; Ci, Zhen, and the others were also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew this came from Wang Zhi; none dared speak for Zhong, and he was dismissed to commoner status; Huang Ci, Li Zhen, and the others were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 直敗，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Zhi fell, Zhong was restored to office and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi fell, Zhong was restored to office and then retired.

sentences.zh: 家居二十六年，至弘治十五年乃卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He lived at home twenty-six years and died only in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for twenty-six years and died in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 忠倜儻多大略，練戎務，強直不阿，敏於政事，故所在著稱。

translations.literal: Zhong was unconventional and possessed great strategic vision, skilled in military affairs, forceful and upright without bending, and quick in administration; therefore wherever he served he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was unconventional and far-sighted, skilled in military affairs, forceful and upright, and quick in administration; wherever he served he won renown.

sentences.zh: 子經，經子錫，錫子治元，皆舉進士。

translations.literal: His son Jing, Jing's son Xi, and Xi's son Zhiyuan all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, Jing's son Xi, and Xi's son Zhiyuan all became jinshi.

sentences.zh: 經，江西參政。

translations.literal: Jing was administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing served as administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 錫，南京光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Xi was director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 治元，員外郎。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was a vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan served as a vice-director.

sentences.zh: 韓雍，字永熙，長洲人。

translations.literal: Han Yong, styled Yongxi, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yong, whose courtesy name was Yongxi, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 負氣果敢，以才略稱。

translations.literal: He was proud in spirit, bold and resolute, and was known for talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and resolute, he was known for his talent and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 錄囚南畿。

translations.literal: He reviewed prisoners in the southern metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed criminal cases in the southern metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 碭山教諭某笞膳夫，膳夫逃匿，父訴教諭殺其子，取他屍支解以證。

translations.literal: A director of studies in Dangshan beat a cook; the cook fled and hid; the father sued the director for killing his son, took another corpse, dismembered it as proof.
translations.idiomatic: A director of studies in Dangshan beat a cook who fled; the cook's father accused the director of murder, dismembered another corpse to fabricate evidence.

sentences.zh: 既誣服，雍蹤跡得之，白其冤。

translations.literal: After a false confession had been obtained, Yong tracked him down by his trail and cleared the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: After a false confession had been extracted, Yong tracked the cook down and cleared the injustice.

sentences.zh: 出巡河道。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the waterways on inspection.

sentences.zh: 已，巡按江西，黜貪墨吏五十七人。

translations.literal: Later, as touring censor of Jiangxi, he dismissed fifty-seven corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as touring censor of Jiangxi, he dismissed fifty-seven corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 廬陵、太和盜起，捕誅之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Luling and Taihe; he captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Luling and Taihe, he captured and executed them.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，處州賊葉宗留自福建轉犯江西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year the bandit Ye Zongliu of Chuzhou turned from Fujian to attack Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year the Chuzhou rebel Ye Zongliu turned from Fujian to raid Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 官軍不利，都督僉事陳榮、指揮劉真遇伏死。

translations.literal: Government troops fared poorly; the regional commander Chen Rong and the commander Liu Zhen met ambush and died.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fared poorly; Regional Commander Chen Rong and Commander Liu Zhen were ambushed and killed.

sentences.zh: 詔雍及鎮守侍郎楊寧督軍民協守。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yong together with the defending vice-minister Yang Ning to supervise troops and civilians in joint defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Defending Vice-Minister Yang Ning were ordered to coordinate troops and civilians in defense.

sentences.zh: 會福建巡按御史汪澄牒鄰境會討賊鄧茂七，俄以賊議降，止兵。

translations.literal: It happened that the Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng sent a dispatch to neighboring districts to join in suppressing the bandit Deng Maoqi; soon, on word that the bandits wished to surrender, he halted the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng had called neighboring districts to join against the rebel Deng Maoqi, but soon halted the army when the rebels offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「賊果降，退未晚也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "If the bandits truly surrender, it will not be too late to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "If they truly surrender, we can withdraw then—it is not too late."

sentences.zh: 」趨進，賊已叛，澄坐得罪死。

translations.literal: He pressed forward; the bandits had already rebelled again, and Cheng was punished by death for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward, but the rebels had already rebelled again; Wang Cheng was executed for his error.

sentences.zh: 人以是服雍識。

translations.literal: People therefore admired Yong's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: People admired Yong's judgment from this episode.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年擢廣東副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he was promoted to vice-commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he was promoted to vice-commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳循薦為右僉都御史，代楊寧巡撫江西。

translations.literal: The grand secretary Chen Xun recommended him as right vice censor-in-chief to replace Yang Ning as grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Xun recommended him as right vice censor-in-chief to replace Yang Ning as grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏免秋糧。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he memorialized to remit the autumn grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he secured remission of the autumn grain tax.

sentences.zh: 劾奏寧王不法事，王府官皆得罪。

translations.literal: He impeached and reported the unlawful conduct of the Prince of Ning; all the princely establishment officials were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Prince of Ning for unlawful conduct, and all the princely establishment officials were punished.

sentences.zh: 時雍年甫三十，赫然有才望，所規畫措置，鹹可為後法。

translations.literal: At that time Yong was only thirty years old, already illustrious in talent and reputation; whatever he planned and arranged could all serve as models for later.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was only thirty, yet already renowned for talent; his plans and measures became models for later administrators.

sentences.zh: 天順初，罷天下巡撫官，改山西副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun the empire's grand coordinators were abolished and he was changed to vice-commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign the empire's grand coordinators were abolished, and Yong was transferred to vice-commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 寧王以前憾劾其擅乘肩輿諸事，下獄，奪官。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, nursing an old grudge, impeached him for unauthorized use of a sedan chair and other matters; he was imprisoned and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, nursing an old grudge, impeached him for unauthorized use of a sedan chair; Yong was imprisoned and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 起大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was raised to vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 尋復為右僉都御史，佐寇深理院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made right vice censor-in-chief to assist Kou Shen in administering the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as right vice censor-in-chief to assist Kou Shen in running the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 石亨既誅，錦衣指揮劉敬坐飯亨直房，用朋黨律論死。

translations.literal: After Shi Heng was executed, the Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Liu Jing was sentenced to death under the statute on factions for dining in Heng's private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Heng was executed, Embroidered Guard Commander Liu Jing was sentenced to death under the faction statute for dining in Heng's private quarters.

sentences.zh: 雍言：「律重朋黨，謂阿比亂朝政也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "The law treats factions severely because it means forming cliques to disrupt court governance."
translations.idiomatic: Yong argued, "The law treats factions severely because it means forming cliques to disrupt court governance."

sentences.zh: 以一飯當之，豈律意？

translations.literal: To apply that to a single meal—can that be the law's intent?
translations.idiomatic: To apply that to a single meal—can that be what the law intends?

sentences.zh: 且亨盛時大臣朝夕趨門，不坐，獨坐敬何也？

translations.literal: Moreover, when Heng was at his height great ministers hurried to his gate morning and evening and were not punished—why punish Jing alone?
translations.idiomatic: When Heng was at his height, great ministers visited him daily without punishment—why punish Jing alone for one meal?

sentences.zh: 」深嘆服，出之。

translations.literal: Shen sighed in admiration and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Shen sighed in admiration and released him.

sentences.zh: 母憂，起復。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he was recalled from mourning to office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to office.

sentences.zh: 四年，巡撫宣府、大同。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was grand coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as grand coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 七年議事入覲，帝壯其貌，留為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he came to court to discuss affairs; the emperor admired his bearing and kept him as right vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he came to court to discuss affairs; the emperor admired his bearing and kept him as right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 雍馳至南京，集諸將議方略。

translations.literal: Yong galloped to Nanjing and gathered the generals to discuss strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yong galloped to Nanjing and gathered the generals to plan strategy.

sentences.zh: 先是，編修邱濬上書大學士李賢，言賊在廣東者宜驅，在廣西者宜困。

translations.literal: Earlier, the compiler Qiu Jun wrote to the grand secretary Li Xian, saying that rebels in Guangdong should be driven out and those in Guangxi should be hemmed in.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Compiler Qiu Jun had written to Grand Secretary Li Xian arguing that rebels in Guangdong should be driven out and those in Guangxi should be hemmed in.

sentences.zh: 欲宿兵大藤峽，扼其出入，蹂其禾稼，期一二年盡賊。

translations.literal: He wished to station troops at Dateng Gorge, choke their exits and entrances, trample their grain crops, and expect to exterminate the bandits in one or two years.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed stationing troops at Dateng Gorge to block their movements, destroy their crops, and exterminate the rebels within a year or two.

sentences.zh: 賢善之，獻於朝，詔錄示諸將。

translations.literal: Xian approved it, presented it at court, and an edict ordered it copied and shown to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian approved the plan, presented it at court, and an edict ordered it copied for the generals.

sentences.zh: 諸將主其說，請令遊擊將軍和勇率番騎趨廣東，而大軍直趨廣西，分兵撲滅。

translations.literal: The generals upheld his plan and requested that the mobile commander He Yong lead tribal cavalry toward Guangdong while the main army went straight to Guangxi and divided forces to stamp them out.
translations.idiomatic: The generals favored this plan, proposing that Mobile Commander He Yong lead tribal cavalry into Guangdong while the main army marched into Guangxi to stamp out the rebels in separate columns.

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「賊已蔓延數千里，而所至與戰，是自敝也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "The bandits have already spread over several thousand li; to fight wherever we reach is to wear ourselves out."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "The rebels have spread over thousands of li; fighting wherever we find them will only exhaust us."

sentences.zh: 當全師直搗大藤峽。

translations.literal: We should concentrate the whole army and strike straight at Dateng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: We should concentrate the entire army and strike straight at Dateng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 南可援高、肇、雷、廉；

translations.literal: To the south we can support Gao, Zhao, Lei, and Lian;
translations.idiomatic: To the south we can support Gao, Zhao, Lei, and Lian;

sentences.zh: 東可應南、韶；

translations.literal: to the east we can respond to Nan and Shao;
translations.idiomatic: to the east we can respond to Nanxiong and Shaozhou;

sentences.zh: 西可取柳、慶；

translations.literal: to the west we can take Liu and Qing;
translations.idiomatic: to the west we can take Liuzhou and Qingzhou;

sentences.zh: 北可斷陽峒諸路。

translations.literal: to the north we can cut off the routes of Yangdong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: to the north we can cut off the Yangdong routes.

sentences.zh: 首尾相應，攻其腹心。

translations.literal: Head and tail will answer each other as we strike their vital center.
translations.idiomatic: With head and tail coordinated, we strike at their heart.

sentences.zh: 巢穴既傾，余迎刃解耳。

translations.literal: Once the nest is overturned, the rest will fall apart like splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Once the nest is destroyed, the rest will fall apart easily.

sentences.zh: 舍此不圖，而分兵四出，賊益奔突，郡邑益殘，所謂救火而噓之也。

translations.literal: To abandon this plan and divide the army in four directions will make the bandits run all the more, counties and prefectures suffer all the more—what is called trying to put out a fire while blowing on it.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this and divide our forces in four directions would only let the rebels run wild and devastate more districts—it would be like trying to put out a fire while blowing on it.

sentences.zh: 」眾曰「善。

translations.literal: The assembly said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」輔亦知雍才足辦賊，軍謀一聽雍。

translations.literal: Fu also knew Yong's talent was sufficient to handle the bandits, and military planning was left entirely to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu also knew Yong was capable of finishing the campaign, and left all military planning to him.

sentences.zh: 雍等遂倍道趨全州。

translations.literal: Yong and the others then marched by double stages to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his forces then marched at forced pace to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 陽峒苗掠興安，擊破之。

translations.literal: Miao of Yangdong raided Xing'an; they attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangdong Miao raided Xing'an, they attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 至桂林，斬失機指揮李英等四人以徇。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Guilin, he beheaded the negligent commander Li Ying and three others as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guilin, he had Commander Li Ying and three other officers who had missed their chance beheaded as an object lesson.

sentences.zh: 按地圖與諸將議曰：「賊以修仁、荔浦為羽翼，當先收二縣以孤賊勢。

translations.literal: Consulting the map, he discussed with the generals, saying: "The bandits use Xiuren and Lipu as wings; we should first take the two counties to isolate the bandits' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Studying the map, he conferenced with his generals: "The rebels use Xiuren and Lipu as their wings; we must seize those two counties first to isolate their power.

sentences.zh: 」乃督兵十六萬人，分五道，先破修仁賊，窮追至力山。

translations.literal: He then supervised an army of 160,000 men, divided into five routes, first defeated the Xiuren bandits, and pursued relentlessly to Lishan.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered 160,000 troops in five columns, smashed the Xiuren rebels first, and pursued them all the way to Lishan.

sentences.zh: 擒千二百余人，斬首七千三百級。

translations.literal: They captured more than 1,200 persons and severed 7,300 heads.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than 1,200 prisoners and counted 7,300 enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 荔浦亦定。

translations.literal: Lipu was also pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lipu was pacified as well.

sentences.zh: 十月至潯州，延問父老，皆曰：「峽，天險，不可攻，宜以計困。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he arrived at Xunzhou, summoned and questioned the elders, who all said: "The gorge is a natural barrier; it cannot be attacked—we should use stratagem to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Xunzhou and asked the local elders, who all said, "The gorge is impregnable by nature; do not assault it—use stratagem to wear the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 」雍曰：「峽延廣六百餘里，安能使困？

translations.literal: Yong said: "The gorge extends more than 600 li—how could we make them hemmed in?
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, "The gorge stretches more than six hundred li—how can we possibly hem them in?

sentences.zh: 兵分則力弱，師老則財匱，賊何時得平？

translations.literal: If troops are divided, strength is weak; if the army ages, supplies are exhausted—when will the bandits be pacified?
translations.idiomatic: Dividing our forces weakens us; a prolonged campaign exhausts our funds—when would the rebels ever be pacified?

sentences.zh: 吾計決矣。

translations.literal: My plan is settled.
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 」遂長驅至峽口。

translations.literal: He then drove straight to the mouth of the gorge.
translations.idiomatic: He marched straight to the gorge mouth.

sentences.zh: 儒生、裏老數十人伏道左，願為向導。

translations.literal: Several dozen literati and village elders crouched by the left of the road, offering to serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of scholars and village elders waited by the roadside, offering to guide the army.

sentences.zh: 雍見即罵曰：「賊敢紿我！

translations.literal: Yong saw them and at once cursed: "Bandits dare to deceive me!
translations.idiomatic: Yong spotted them and immediately shouted, "You rebels dare try to fool me!

sentences.zh: 」叱左右縛斬之，左右皆愕，既縛，而袂中利刃出。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to bind and behead them; the attendants were all startled; once bound, sharp blades emerged from their sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to seize and execute them. His attendants were astonished—but once bound, blades appeared from their sleeves.

sentences.zh: 推問，果賊也。

translations.literal: On interrogation, they were indeed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation, they proved to be rebels in disguise.

sentences.zh: 悉支解刳腸胃，分掛林箐中，累累相屬。

translations.literal: All were dismembered, their bellies cut open, and hung piecemeal in the forest thickets, one after another in strings.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all dismembered and disemboweled, the parts hung in clusters through the woods.

sentences.zh: 賊大驚曰：「韓公天神也！

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly alarmed and said: "Lord Han is a heavenly god!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were terrified: "Marshal Han is a god!

sentences.zh: 」雍令總兵官歐信等為五哨，自象州、武宣攻其北；

translations.literal: Yong ordered the commander-in-chief Ou Xin and others to form five squads and attack from the north via Xiangzhou and Wuxuan;
translations.idiomatic: Yong assigned Commander Ou Xin to five squads attacking from the north through Xiangzhou and Wuxuan;

sentences.zh: 身與輔督都指揮白全等為八哨，自桂平、平南攻其南；

translations.literal: he himself, with Fu supervising regional commander Bai Quan and others in eight squads, attacked from the south via Guiping and Pingnan;
translations.idiomatic: he himself, with Wang Fu supervising Regional Commander Bai Quan in eight squads, struck from the south through Guiping and Pingnan;

sentences.zh: 參將孫震等為二哨，從水路入；

translations.literal: assistant commander Sun Zhen and others formed two squads and entered by water;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Sun Zhen led two squads in by water;

sentences.zh: 而別分兵守諸隘口。

translations.literal: while other forces were separately stationed to guard the passes.
translations.idiomatic: while other detachments held the passes.

sentences.zh: 賊魁侯大狗等大懼，先移其累重於桂州橫石塘，而立柵南山，多置滾木、礧石、鏢槍、藥弩拒官軍。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftains Hou Dagou and the rest were greatly afraid; they first moved their families and baggage to Hengshi Pond in Guizhou, and built stockades on the southern mountain with many rolling logs, rolled stones, barbed spears, and poisoned crossbows to repel the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Hou Dagou and his lieutenants were terrified. They moved their families and supplies to Hengshi Pond near Guizhou and fortified the southern hills with rolling logs, boulders, hooked spears, and poisoned crossbows to hold off the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 十二月朔，雍等督諸軍水陸並進，擁團牌登山，殊死戰。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, Yong and others directed all armies to advance together by land and water, carrying round shields up the mountain in a desperate battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, Yong led a combined land-and-water assault; troops bore round shields up the slopes and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 連破石門、林峒、沙田、古營諸巢，焚其室廬積聚，賊皆奔潰。

translations.literal: They successively broke the nests at Shimen, Lindong, Shatian, Guying, and elsewhere, burned their dwellings and stores, and the bandits all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed nest after nest at Shimen, Lindong, Shatian, and Guying, burned dwellings and stockpiles, and the rebels fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 伐木開道，直抵橫石塘及九層樓諸山。

translations.literal: Felling trees to open paths, they went straight to Hengshi Pond and the mountains of Jiuceng Tower and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting roads through the forest, they pressed on to Hengshi Pond and the Jiuceng Tower heights.

sentences.zh: 賊復立柵數重，憑高以拒。

translations.literal: The bandits again erected several layers of stockades and relied on the heights to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw up line after line of stockades on the heights.

sentences.zh: 官軍誘賊發矢石，度且盡，雍躬督諸軍緣木攀藤上。

translations.literal: The government army lured the bandits to shoot arrows and stones, estimated they were nearly exhausted, and Yong personally directed the armies to climb trees and vines.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces baited the rebels into expending their missiles; when Yong judged the supply nearly spent, he led the troops up cliffs by tree and vine.

sentences.zh: 別遣壯士從間道先登，據山頂舉炮。

translations.literal: He separately sent stalwarts by a hidden path to climb first, seize the mountaintop, and fire cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops crept up a hidden path, seized the summit, and opened fire with cannon.

sentences.zh: 賊不能支，遂大敗。

translations.literal: The bandits could not hold and were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could not hold and were routed.

sentences.zh: 先後破賊三百二十四寨，生擒大狗及其黨七百八十人，斬首三千二百有奇，墜溺死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: In all they broke 324 bandit stockades, captured Hou Dagou and his followers alive—780 persons—and severed more than 3,200 heads; those who fell or drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took 324 rebel strongholds, captured Hou Dagou and 780 of his men alive, counted more than 3,200 heads, and countless more who fell or drowned.

sentences.zh: 峽有大藤如虹，橫亙兩厓間。

translations.literal: In the gorge was a great vine like a rainbow, spanning between the two cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: A great vine like a rainbow bridged the two cliffs.

sentences.zh: 雍斧斷之，改名斷藤峽，勒石紀功而還。

translations.literal: Yong cut it with an axe, renamed the place Broken Vine Gorge, carved a stone to record merit, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yong severed it with an axe, renamed the gorge Broken Vine Gorge, inscribed a victory stele, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 分兵擊余黨，郁林、陽江、洛容、博白次第皆定。

translations.literal: Dividing troops to strike the remaining followers, Yulin, Yangjiang, Luorong, and Bobai were pacified in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Detachments mopped up the remaining rebels, and Yulin, Yangjiang, Luorong, and Bobai were pacified one after another.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，賜敕嘉勞，召輔等還，遷雍左副都御史，提督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, granted an edict of praise and reward, summoned Fu and the rest back, promoted Yong to left vice censor-in-chief, and made him overseer of the military affairs of the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, sent a commendatory edict, recalled Wang Fu and his staff, promoted Yong to left vice censor-in-chief, and put him in charge of military affairs in the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 雍乃散遣諸軍，以省饋餉。

translations.literal: Yong then dispersed the armies to economize on supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then sent the armies home to save on provisioning.

sentences.zh: 而遺孽侯鄭昂等遂乘虛陷潯州及洛容、北流二縣。

translations.literal: But the remnant bandits Hou Zheng'ang and others then took advantage of the void and seized Xunzhou and the two counties Luorong and Beiliu.
translations.idiomatic: But remnant rebels led by Hou Zheng'ang seized the moment, overrunning Xunzhou and the counties of Luorong and Beiliu.

sentences.zh: 雍被劾引罪，帝宥之。

translations.literal: Yong was impeached and acknowledged guilt; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was impeached and accepted blame, but the emperor excused him.

sentences.zh: 雍益發兵撲討。

translations.literal: Yong further raised troops to hunt them down.
translations.idiomatic: Yong raised more troops to crush them.

sentences.zh: 時諸賊所在蜂起，思恩、潯、賓、柳城悉被擾掠。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere like bees; Si'en, Xun, Bin, and Liucheng were all raided.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were springing up everywhere; Si'en, Xunzhou, Binzhou, and Liucheng all suffered raids.

sentences.zh: 流劫至廣東，欽、化二州皆應時破殄。

translations.literal: Raiders swept as far as Guangdong; Qin and Hua, the two prefectures, were both destroyed in due time.
translations.idiomatic: Raids reached into Guangdong; the prefectures of Qinzhou and Huazhou were crushed in turn.

sentences.zh: 四年春，雍以兩廣地大事殷，請東西各設巡撫，帝可之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Yong, because the two Guang were vast in territory and heavy in affairs, requested that east and west each have a grand coordinator; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Yong argued that the two provinces were too large and busy for one man, and asked to split them with separate grand coordinators for east and west; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 命陳濂撫廣東，張鵬撫廣西，而雍專理軍事。

translations.literal: Chen Lian was ordered to coordinate Guangdong, Zhang Peng to coordinate Guangxi, while Yong specialized in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lian was appointed to Guangdong, Zhang Peng to Guangxi, while Yong retained military command alone.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon, on mourning he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went home on bereavement leave.

sentences.zh: 明年，兩廣盜復起，僉事陶魯言：「兩廣地勢錯互，當如臂指相使，不可離析。

translations.literal: The next year, bandits in the two Guang rose again; the vice prefect Tao Lu said: "The terrain of the two Guang is interlocking; they should operate like arm and fingers together—it cannot be split apart.
translations.idiomatic: The following year banditry flared again. Vice Prefect Tao Lu wrote: "The two provinces' terrain is intertwined; they must work like arm and fingers in concert and cannot be split apart.

sentences.zh: 近賊犯廣西，臣與廣東三司議調兵，匝月未決，盜賊無所憚。

translations.literal: Lately when bandits invaded Guangxi, I and the three offices of Guangdong discussed moving troops; for a full month no decision was made, and the robbers had nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels lately struck Guangxi, the Guangdong administration and I spent a month debating troop transfers, and the bandits lost all fear of us.

sentences.zh: 乞仍命大臣總督便。

translations.literal: I beg that a great minister still be ordered to oversee all—it would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Please restore a supervising minister with overall command.

sentences.zh: 」會僉事林錦、巡按御史龔晟亦以為請。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Prefect Lin Jin and touring investigating censor Gong Sheng also requested the same.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Prefect Lin Jin and Investigating Censor Gong Sheng made the same request.

sentences.zh: 乃罷兩巡撫，而起復雍右都御史，總督如故。

translations.literal: The two grand coordinators were abolished, and Yong was recalled from mourning as right censor-in-chief, general supervisor as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished the dual grand coordinators and recalled Yong from mourning as right censor-in-chief with his former overall command restored.

sentences.zh: 又明年正月，雍疏辭新命，乞終制，不許。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year again, Yong memorialized declining the new appointment and begging to complete mourning; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Yong asked to decline the appointment and finish mourning; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 雍抵任，遣參將張壽、遊擊馮昇等分道討賊，忻州八寨蠻及諸山瑤、僮掠州縣者，皆摧破之。

translations.literal: Yong arrived at his post, sent assistant commanders Zhang Shou, mobile commander Feng Sheng, and others on separate routes to pursue bandits, and crushed the eight-stockade barbarians of Xinzhou and the Yao and Zhuang of the mountains who raided prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yong took up his post and sent Assistant Commander Zhang Shou and Mobile Commander Feng Sheng against the rebels in several columns, shattering the Xinzhou eight-stockade tribes and the mountain Yao and Zhuang who had been raiding the districts.

sentences.zh: 蠻民素懾雍威，寇盜浸息。

translations.literal: The barbarian peoples had long feared Yong's authority; raiders and bandits gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples who had long feared Yong's prestige quieted down, and banditry gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 九年，柳、潯諸蠻復叛，參將楊廣等俘斬九百人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the barbarians of Liu, Xun, and elsewhere rebelled again; assistant commander Yang Guang and others captured and beheaded 900 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year tribes in Liuzhou and Xunzhou rebelled again; Assistant Commander Yang Guang took nine hundred heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 方更進，而賊破懷集縣。

translations.literal: Just as they were advancing further, bandits broke Huaiji County.
translations.idiomatic: While government forces were pressing forward, rebels smashed Huaiji County.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾雍奏報不實。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached Yong for untruthful reports.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached Yong for misreporting the situation.

sentences.zh: 廣西鎮守中官黃沁素憾雍抑己，因訐雍，且言其貪欲縱酒，濫賞妄費。

translations.literal: The Guangxi garrison eunuch Huang Qin had long resented Yong for restraining him; he therefore denounced Yong, also saying he was greedy, indulged in wine, and gave rewards and spent recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi garrison eunuch Huang Qin, who had long resented Yong's restraints, denounced him as greedy and dissolute, accusing him of lavishing reckless rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝遣給事中張謙等往勘。

translations.literal: The emperor sent supervising secretary Zhang Qian and others to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Supervising Secretary Zhang Qian and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 而廣西布政使何宜、副使張斅銜雍素輕己，共醞釀其罪。

translations.literal: But Guangxi provincial administration commissioner He Yi and vice commissioner Zhang Xiao bore a grudge that Yong had always looked down on them; together they brewed up charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Provincial Administration Commissioner He Yi and Vice Commissioner Zhang Xiao, who felt Yong had always slighted them, helped manufacture the charges.

sentences.zh: 謙還奏，事虛實交半，竟命致仕去。

translations.literal: Qian returned and reported; affairs were half false and half true, and in the end he was ordered to retire from office and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian reported back that the charges were half true and half false; the emperor ordered Yong to retire.

sentences.zh: 雍洞達闿爽，重信義。

translations.literal: Yong was penetrating in understanding, open and forthright, and valued faith and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was perceptive and forthright, and valued loyalty and honor.

sentences.zh: 撫江西時，請追謚文天祥、謝枋得。

translations.literal: When he was coordinator of Jiangxi, he requested posthumous titles for Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as coordinator of Jiangxi, he petitioned for posthumous honors for Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde.

sentences.zh: 詔謚天祥忠烈、枋得文節。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed on Tianxiang the posthumous name Loyal and Stern, on Fangde Literary Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded Tianxiang the posthumous title "Loyal and Stern" and Fangde "Literary Integrity."

sentences.zh: 有雄略，善斷，動中事機。

translations.literal: He had bold strategy, was good at decisions, and his actions hit the crux of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had bold strategic vision, decisive judgment, and a knack for timing.

sentences.zh: 臨戰，率躬親矢石，不目瞬。

translations.literal: In battle he always went in person under arrows and stones without blinking an eye.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he always led from the front under arrow and stone fire without flinching.

sentences.zh: 自奉尊嚴，三司皆長跪白事。

translations.literal: He maintained his own dignity; the three offices all knelt long to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with stern dignity; the three provincial offices all knelt to report to him.

sentences.zh: 軍門設銅鼓數十，儀節詳密。

translations.literal: At the military gate he set up several dozen bronze drums; ceremony and protocol were detailed and strict.
translations.idiomatic: His headquarters boasted dozens of bronze drums, and his protocol was meticulously observed.

sentences.zh: 裨將以下，繩柙無所假。

translations.literal: For assistant generals and below, the rope cage had no tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officers enjoyed no slack whatsoever in discipline.

sentences.zh: 兩地鎮守宦官素驕恣，亦惕息無敢肆。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuchs of both regions were normally arrogant and willful; they too were cautious and breathed softly, not daring to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Even the notoriously arrogant garrison eunuchs in both provinces behaved themselves and dared not act out.

sentences.zh: 疾惡嚴，坦中不為崖岸，揮斥財帛不少惜。

translations.literal: He hated evil strictly; his heart was level and made no steep banks; he threw out money and goods without sparing.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce toward wrongdoing, unpretentious in manner, and spent money freely without counting the cost.

sentences.zh: 故雖令行禁止，民得安堵，而謗議亦易起。

translations.literal: Therefore although orders went forth and prohibitions stood, the people could live in peace, yet slander and criticism also arose easily.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rule brought order and the people peace, criticism came easily.

sentences.zh: 為中官所齮龁，公論皆不平。

translations.literal: He was gnawed at by eunuchs; public opinion everywhere was indignant on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs undermined him, and public opinion rallied to his defense.

sentences.zh: 兩廣人念雍功，尤惜其去，為立祠祀焉。

translations.literal: The people of the two Guang remembered Yong's achievements, especially regretted his departure, and erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the two provinces cherished his achievements, mourned his dismissal, and erected temples in his honor.

sentences.zh: 家居五年卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: At home for five years he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home five years later, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 正德間，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he was posthumously titled Xiang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he received the posthumous title "Able and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 初以軍功予一子錦衣百戶，雍以授其弟睦。

translations.literal: At first for military merit one son was granted an Imperial Guard centurion post; Yong gave it to his younger brother Mu.
translations.idiomatic: An initial military reward had granted his son a post in the Imperial Guard as company commander; Yong gave it to his younger brother Mu instead.

sentences.zh: 至是，錄一子國子生。

translations.literal: At this time one son was enrolled as an Imperial Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion one son was enrolled in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 余子俊，字士英，青神人。

translations.literal: Yu Zijun, styled Shiying, was a native of Qingshen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun, styled Shiying, was a native of Qingshen.

sentences.zh: 父祥，戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Xiang was a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang served as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子俊舉景泰二年進士，授戶部主事，進員外郎。
