translations.literal: Zijun passed the civil examinations in the second year of the Jingtai reign, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and advanced to assistant department director.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and rose to assistant department director.

sentences.zh: 在部十年，以廉幹稱。

translations.literal: He spent ten years in the ministry and was known for integrity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten years in the ministry and earned a reputation for integrity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 出為西安知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發廩十萬石振貸。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he released 100,000 shi from the granary for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, he released a hundred thousand shi of grain from the public granaries for relief loans.

sentences.zh: 區畫以償，官不損而民濟。

translations.literal: He planned repayment arrangements; the government did not suffer loss and the people were aided.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged repayment so the treasury suffered no loss while the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 成化初，所司上治行當旌者，知府十人，而子俊為首。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign the responsible offices reported administrators worthy of commendation—ten prefects, with Zijun first.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign the responsible offices nominated administrators for commendation—ten prefects, with Zijun ranked first.

sentences.zh: 以林聰薦，為陜西右參政，歲餘擢右布政使。

translations.literal: On Lin Cong's recommendation he became right regional vice commissioner in Shaanxi, and after a little more than a year was promoted to right provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On Lin Cong's recommendation he became right vice commissioner in Shaanxi, and a little over a year later was promoted to right provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年轉左，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the left and shifted to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the left post and reassigned to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 甫半載，拜右副都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: After only half a year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: After only half a year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 先是，巡撫王銳請沿邊築墻建堡，為久遠計，工未興而罷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Coordinator Wang Rui had requested building walls and forts along the border as a long-term plan; the work had not begun before it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand Coordinator Wang Rui had proposed building walls and forts along the border as a long-term plan, but the project was halted before work began.

sentences.zh: 子俊上疏言：「三邊惟延慶地平易，利馳突。

translations.literal: Zijun memorialized, saying: "Of the three borders, only the Yanqing region has level ground, favorable for cavalry raids.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun memorialized: "Of the three border regions, only Yanqing has level terrain favorable to cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 寇屢入犯，獲邊人為導，徑入河套屯牧。

translations.literal: Bandits repeatedly invaded, captured border people as guides, and went straight into the Ordos bend to pasture herds.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders invaded repeatedly, seized border people as guides, and drove straight into the Ordos bend to pasture their herds.

sentences.zh: 自是寇顧居內，我反屯外，急宜於沿邊築墻置堡。

translations.literal: From this the bandits came to dwell within while we camped outside; urgently we should build walls and set forts along the border.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the enemy has settled inside while we camp outside; we must urgently build walls and forts along the border.

sentences.zh: 況今舊界石所在，多高山陡厓。

translations.literal: Moreover, where the old boundary stones stand, there are mostly lofty mountains and steep cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, where the old boundary markers stand, there are mostly high mountains and steep cliffs.

sentences.zh: 依山形，隨地勢，或鏟削，或壘築，或挑塹，綿引相接，以成邊墻，於計為便。

translations.literal: Following mountain form and ground contours—sometimes cutting away, sometimes piling up, sometimes digging ditches, linked in continuous extension to form a border wall—is convenient in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Following the terrain—cutting slopes, piling earthworks, or digging ditches in continuous stretches to form a border wall—is the most practical approach.

sentences.zh: 」尚書白圭以陜民方困，奏緩役。

translations.literal: Minister Bai Gui, because Shaanxi people were then in distress, memorialized to slow the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Bai Gui, citing the distress of the Shaanxi populace, memorialized to defer the project.

sentences.zh: 既而寇入孤山堡，復犯榆林，子俊先後與朱永、許寧擊敗之。

translations.literal: Before long bandits entered Gushan Fort and again invaded Yulin; Zijun successively, with Zhu Yong and Xu Ning, attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long raiders entered Gushan Fort and again invaded Yulin; Zijun, together with Zhu Yong and Xu Ning, defeated them in successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 是時，寇據河套，歲發大軍征討，卒無功。

translations.literal: At this time bandits held the Ordos bend; each year a great army was sent on campaign, but in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the enemy held the Ordos bend; each year a great army was sent on campaign, yet none succeeded.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，子俊復言：「今征套士馬屯延綏者八萬，芻茭煩內地。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year Zijun again said: "Now in the campaign against the Ordos, 80,000 soldiers and horses are stationed in Yan-Sui, and fodder burdens the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year Zijun again wrote: "The campaign against the Ordos has eighty thousand troops and horses stationed in Yan-Sui, and fodder requisitions are exhausting the interior.

sentences.zh: 若今冬寇不北去，又須備來年軍資。

translations.literal: If this winter the bandits do not go north, we must again prepare next year's military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: If the raiders do not withdraw north this winter, we must again stock supplies for next year's campaign.

sentences.zh: 姑以今年之數約之，米豆需銀九十四萬，草六十萬。

translations.literal: For now estimating from this year's figures, grain and beans require 940,000 in silver, hay 600,000.
translations.idiomatic: Even by this year's figures alone, grain and beans will require nine hundred forty thousand taels of silver, and hay six hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 每人運米豆六斗、草四束，應用四百七萬人，約費行資八百二十五萬。

translations.literal: Per person carrying six dou of grain and beans and four bundles of hay, we would need 4.7 million men, costing about 8.25 million in travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At six dou of grain and beans and four bundles of hay per carrier, we would need four million seven hundred thousand men, with transport costs of about eight million two hundred fifty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 公私煩擾至此，安得不變計。

translations.literal: Public and private trouble to this extent—how can we not change the plan?
translations.idiomatic: With public and private resources strained to this degree, how can we not change our strategy?

sentences.zh: 臣前請築墻建堡，詔事寧舉行。

translations.literal: I previously requested building walls and forts; an edict ordered implementation when affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: I previously requested building walls and forts; an edict ordered the work carried out once affairs were settled.

sentences.zh: 請於明年春夏寇馬疲乏時，役陜西運糧民五萬，給食興工，期兩月畢事。

translations.literal: I ask that next spring and summer, when the raiders' horses are weary, fifty thousand Shaanxi grain-transport laborers be impressed, given rations to start work, with completion expected in two months.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that next spring and summer, when the enemy's horses are exhausted, fifty thousand Shaanxi men who haul grain be conscripted, fed, and set to work, with the project finished within two months.

sentences.zh: 」圭猶持前議阻之。

translations.literal: " Gui still held to his earlier view and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: " Bai Gui still clung to his earlier position and blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 帝是子俊言，命速舉。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed with Zijun's words and ordered swift implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Zijun and ordered the work carried out at once.

sentences.zh: 子俊先用軍功進左副都御史。

translations.literal: Zijun was first advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief on military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun was first promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief on the strength of his military achievements.

sentences.zh: 明年，又用紅鹽池搗巢功，進右都御史。

translations.literal: The next year, again on the merit of raiding the nest at Red Salt Pool, he was advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on the merit of striking the enemy's base at Red Salt Pool, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 寇以搗巢故遠徙，不敢復居套。

translations.literal: The raiders, because of the nest-raid, migrated far away and did not dare dwell again in the Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders, having had their base destroyed, moved far away and no longer dared occupy the Ordos bend.

sentences.zh: 內地患稍息，子俊得一意興役。

translations.literal: Trouble in the interior eased somewhat, and Zijun could devote himself wholly to the labor projects.
translations.idiomatic: Threats to the interior eased somewhat, and Zijun was able to devote himself entirely to construction.

sentences.zh: 東起清水營，西抵花馬池，延袤千七百七十里，鑿崖築墻，掘塹其下，連比不絕。

translations.literal: From Qingshui Camp in the east to Huama Pool in the west, extending 1,770 li, he cut cliffs and built walls, dug ditches below, linked continuously without break.
translations.idiomatic: From Qingshui Camp in the east to Huama Pool in the west—a stretch of 1,770 li—he cut into cliffs and raised walls, dug ditches beneath them, and linked the works in an unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 每二三里置敵臺崖寨備巡警。

translations.literal: Every two or three li he placed beacon towers and cliff forts for patrol and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Every two or three li he built beacon towers and cliff fortresses for patrol and lookout.

sentences.zh: 又於崖寨空處築短墻，橫一斜二如箕狀，以瞭敵避射。

translations.literal: Also at empty spots in cliff forts he built short walls, one horizontal and two slanted like a winnowing basket, to observe the enemy and avoid arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Where cliff fortresses had open ground, he also built low parapets in a winnowing-basket pattern—one horizontal beam and two slanting sides—to watch the enemy and shelter from arrows.

sentences.zh: 凡築城堡十一，邊墩十五，小墩七十八，崖寨八百十九，役軍四萬人，不三月而成。

translations.literal: In all he built eleven castles, fifteen border towers, seventy-eight small towers, eight hundred nineteen cliff forts, using forty thousand soldiers; it was completed in less than three months.
translations.idiomatic: In all he built eleven castles, fifteen major beacon towers, seventy-eight minor towers, and eight hundred nineteen cliff fortresses, employing forty thousand troops; the work was finished in under three months.

sentences.zh: 墻內之地悉分屯墾，歲得糧六萬石有奇。

translations.literal: Land within the wall was all divided for garrison farming, yielding more than sixty thousand shi of grain yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Land inside the wall was allotted for garrison farming, which each year produced more than sixty thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 十年閏六月，子俊具上其事，因以母老乞歸，慰留不許。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month of the tenth year Zijun fully reported the matter to the throne; citing his mother's age he begged to retire, but was comforted and retained—permission refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month of the tenth year Zijun submitted a full report on the project and, pleading that his mother was elderly, asked to retire; the court comforted him and refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 初，延綏鎮治綏德州，屬縣米脂、吳堡悉在其外。

translations.literal: At first the Yan-Sui commandery was administered from Suide Prefecture, and subordinate counties Mizhi and Wubao were all outside it.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Yan-Sui command had its seat at Suide Prefecture, while subordinate counties such as Mizhi and Wubao lay entirely beyond its reach.

sentences.zh: 寇以輕騎入掠，鎮兵覺而追之，輒不及，往往得利去。

translations.literal: Raiders entered with light cavalry to plunder; when garrison troops noticed and pursued, they usually could not catch up, and the raiders often got away with their gains.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders swept in on light horse to plunder; garrison troops would discover the attack and give chase, yet almost never overtook them, and the enemy usually escaped with their loot.

sentences.zh: 自子俊徙鎮榆林，增衛益兵，拓城置戍，攻守器畢具，遂為重鎮，寇抄漸稀，軍民得安耕牧焉。

translations.literal: Since Zijun moved the command to Yulin, increased guards and troops, expanded the city and posted garrisons, and had offensive and defensive equipment fully prepared, it became a major stronghold; raiding grew gradually rare, and soldiers and civilians could peacefully farm and herd.
translations.idiomatic: After Zijun transferred the command to Yulin, enlarged the garrisons, expanded the city, posted troops, and equipped it fully for attack and defense, it became a major stronghold; raids grew rare, and soldiers and civilians could farm and herd in peace.

sentences.zh: 十二年十二月移撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year he was transferred to grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year he was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 子俊知西安時，以居民患水泉鹹苦，鑿渠引城西潏河入灌，民利之。

translations.literal: When Zijun was prefect of Xi'an, because residents suffered from brackish bitter springs, he dug a canal to draw the Yu River west of the city for irrigation; the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Xi'an, Zijun found the townspeople troubled by brackish, bitter well water; he dug a canal to channel the Yu River west of the city for irrigation, to the people's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 久而水溢無所泄。

translations.literal: After a long time the water overflowed with nowhere to discharge.
translations.idiomatic: In time the water backed up with nowhere to drain.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃於城西北開渠泄水，使經漢故城達渭。

translations.literal: At this point he opened a canal northwest of the city to drain the water, routing it through the old Han capital city to reach the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Now he opened a drainage canal northwest of the city, sending the water through the ruins of the old Han capital to the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 公私益便，號「余公渠」。

translations.literal: Public and private affairs grew more convenient; it was called the "Yu Gong Canal."
translations.idiomatic: Public and private needs were better served, and the canal was named the Yu Gong Canal.

sentences.zh: 又於涇陽鑿山引水，溉田千余頃。

translations.literal: He also cut through mountains at Jingyang to draw water, irrigating more than a thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He also tunneled through the mountains at Jingyang to bring in water and irrigate more than a thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 通南山道，直抵漢中，以便行旅。

translations.literal: He opened the South Mountain road, reaching Hanzhong direct, to convenience travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a route over the South Mountains straight through to Hanzhong to ease travel.

sentences.zh: 學校、公署圮者悉新之。

translations.literal: Schools and government offices that had collapsed were all renovated.
translations.idiomatic: Every school and government hall in ruins he rebuilt anew.

sentences.zh: 奏免岷、河、洮三衛之戍南方者萬有奇。

translations.literal: He memorialized to exempt more than ten thousand men of the Min, He, and Tao guards garrisoned in the south.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to release more than ten thousand troops of the Min, He, and Tao guards who were garrisoned in the south.

sentences.zh: 易置南北之更戍者六千有奇，就戍本土。

translations.literal: He exchanged more than six thousand rotating north-south garrison troops so they garrisoned their home regions.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned more than six thousand men who rotated between northern and southern garrisons so they could serve on their home soil.

sentences.zh: 岷州栗林羌為寇，子俊潛師設伏擊走之。

translations.literal: The Lilin Qiang of Minzhou raided; Zijun sent troops in secret, set an ambush, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lilin Qiang of Minzhou raided, Zijun moved troops in secret, laid an ambush, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 十三年召為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was summoned to the capital as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 奏申明條例十事，又列上軍功賞格，由是中外有所遵守。

translations.literal: He memorialized clarifying ten regulations, and also submitted military merit reward standards; thereafter court and regions had rules to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to clarify ten regulations and submitted standards for rewarding military merit; from then on the court and the provinces had clear rules to follow.

sentences.zh: 緬甸酋卜剌浪欲奪思洪發貢章地，設詞請於朝。

translations.literal: The Burmese chief Bolalang wished to seize Si Hongfa's tribute-tributary territory and used polite wording in a request to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese chieftain Bolalang sought to seize the tribute domain of Si Hongfa and framed his demand in courteous language to the court.

sentences.zh: 子俊言不宜許，乃諭止之。

translations.literal: Zijun said it should not be granted; the court thereupon instructed refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun argued that the request should be denied, and the court issued instructions to refuse.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫陳儼等以播州苗竊發，請調湖廣、廣西、四川兵五萬，合貴州兵會剿。

translations.literal: The Guizhou grand coordinator Chen Yan and others, because Bozhou Miao had risen in secret, requested deploying fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Guangxi, and Sichuan to join Guizhou forces for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou grand coordinator Chen Yan and others, reporting that Bozhou Miao had risen in secret, asked that fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Guangxi, and Sichuan be mobilized to join Guizhou forces in a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 子俊言賊在四川，而貴州請討，是邀功也，奏寢其事。

translations.literal: Zijun said the bandits were in Sichuan while Guizhou asked to campaign—that was claiming merit—and memorialized to shelve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun observed that the rebels were in Sichuan while Guizhou was asking to lead the campaign—a bid for credit—and memorialized to set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 初，子俊論陳鉞掩殺貢夷罪，帝以汪直故宥之。

translations.literal: At first Zijun had impeached Chen Yue for concealing the killing of tribute tribesmen; the Emperor pardoned him because of Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zijun had denounced Chen Yue for covering up the slaughter of tributary tribesmen; the emperor pardoned Yue on account of the eunuch Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 鉞多方構子俊於直，會母憂歸，得免。

translations.literal: Yue in many ways framed Zijun before Wang Zhi; when Zijun went home for his mother's mourning he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yue repeatedly slandered Zijun to Wang Zhi; Zijun was spared only when he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 子俊之築邊墻也，或疑沙土易傾，寇至未可恃。

translations.literal: When Zijun built the border wall, some doubted that sandy soil would easily collapse and that when raiders came it could not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijun built the border wall, some questioned whether sandy earth would hold and whether the works could be trusted once raiders arrived.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，寇入犯，許寧等逐之。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year raiders entered in invasion; Xu Ning and others pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year raiders invaded again; Xu Ning and others pursued them.

sentences.zh: 寇扼於墻塹，散漫不得出，遂大衄，邊人益思子俊功。

translations.literal: The raiders were blocked by wall and ditch, scattered and unable to exit, and suffered a great defeat; border people increasingly remembered Zijun's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped by the wall and ditch, the raiders were scattered and could not break out; they suffered a crushing defeat, and people on the border came to appreciate Zijun's achievement all the more.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜戶部尚書，尋加太子太保。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue, and soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue and soon thereafter made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十年命兼左副都御史，總督大同、宣府軍務。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered also to serve as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and to supervise military affairs of Datong and Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and to supervise military affairs in Datong and Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 其冬還朝。

translations.literal: That winter he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，星變，陳時弊八事，帝多采納。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year there was a planetary anomaly; he presented eight current abuses; the Emperor adopted many.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, when unusual stars appeared, he submitted eight abuses of the times; the emperor adopted many of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復出行邊。

translations.literal: Before long he again went out to inspect the border.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out again to tour the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，子俊巡歷宣、大，請以延綏邊墻法行之兩鎮，因歲歉而止。

translations.literal: At first, when Zijun toured Xuan and Da, he had asked to apply the Yan-Sui border-wall method in the two commands, but because of a lean harvest year it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zijun had toured Xuanfu and Datong, he had proposed applying the Yan-Sui wall-building method to both commands, but the plan was halted because of a poor harvest.

sentences.zh: 比復出，銳欲行之。

translations.literal: When he went out again he was keen to carry it through.
translations.idiomatic: On this second tour he was determined to see it through.

sentences.zh: 言東起四海冶，西抵黃河，延袤千三百餘里，舊有墩百七十，應增築四百四十，墩高廣皆三丈，計役夫八萬六千，數月可成。

translations.literal: He said from Sihaizhuan in the east to the Yellow River in the west, extending more than 1,300 li, there were 170 old towers and 440 should be added; towers height and breadth each three zhang; estimated laborers eighty-six thousand; could be completed in several months.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a line from Sihaizhuan in the east to the Yellow River in the west—more than 1,300 li in all—with 170 existing towers and 440 to be added, each tower three zhang high and wide, requiring an estimated eighty-six thousand laborers and finishable within a few months.

sentences.zh: 詔明年四月即工。

translations.literal: An edict ordered work to begin in the fourth month of the next year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set the start of work for the fourth month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 然是時，歲比不登，公私耗敝，驟興大役，上下難之。

translations.literal: Yet at that time harvests failed year after year, public and private were exhausted; suddenly launching a great labor project—above and below found it hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet harvests had failed year after year, public and private resources were depleted, and to launch a massive project so suddenly was difficult for everyone, high and low alike.

sentences.zh: 子俊又欲責成於邊臣，而己不親其事。

translations.literal: Zijun also wanted to make border officials responsible while he himself did not personally oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun also wished to hold frontier officials accountable while keeping himself aloof from direct supervision.

sentences.zh: 謗議由是起。

translations.literal: Slander and criticism arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Criticism and slander followed.

sentences.zh: 至冬，疏請還京。

translations.literal: By winter he memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By winter he memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝入蜚語，命改左都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed malicious gossip and ordered him changed to Left Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave credence to malicious rumors and reassigned him as Left Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 中官韋敬讒子俊假修邊多侵耗，又劾子俊私恩怨，易將帥。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wei Jing slandered Zijun, falsely saying repair of the border involved much embezzlement, and also impeached Zijun for private resentments in changing commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wei Jing accused Zijun of gross waste in the border works and also impeached him for swapping commanders out of personal spite.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎阮勤等為白。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Ruan Qin and others spoke in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Ruan Qin and others spoke up in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，讓勤等。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and rebuked Qin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and rebuked Qin and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 而給事、御史復交章劾，中朝多欲傾子俊。

translations.literal: But supervising secretaries and censors again submitted joint impeachments; many at court wished to topple Zijun.
translations.idiomatic: Yet supervising secretaries and censors submitted further joint impeachments, and many at court were eager to bring Zijun down.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎杜謙等往勘，平情按之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Du Qian and others went to investigate and judged impartially.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Du Qian and others were sent to investigate and weighed the charges even-handedly.

sentences.zh: 還奏易置將帥如勤等言，所費無私。

translations.literal: On return they reported that changing commanders was as Qin and others said, and the expenditures involved no private gain.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they reported that the commander changes were as Ruan Qin had described and that Zijun had taken nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 然為銀百五十萬，米菽二百三十萬，耗財煩民，不得無罪。

translations.literal: Yet silver amounted to 1.5 million, grain and beans 2.3 million—wasting wealth and troubling the people—he could not be without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the cost had run to 1.5 million taels of silver and 2.3 million units of grain and beans; such waste and burden on the people could not go entirely unpunished.

sentences.zh: 遂落太子太保，致仕去，時二十二年二月也。

translations.literal: He was therefore stripped of Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired; it was the second month of the twenty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore stripped of his rank as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office in the second month of the twenty-second year.

sentences.zh: 子俊沈毅寡言，有偉略。

translations.literal: Zijun was deep, resolute, and taciturn, with great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zijun was grave, resolute, and sparing of words, yet possessed of great strategic vision.

sentences.zh: 凡奏疏公移，必自屬草，每夜分方寢。

translations.literal: Whatever memorials or official correspondence, he always drafted them himself; he often did not sleep until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Every memorial and dispatch he drafted with his own hand, and he often did not sleep until the middle watch.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「大臣謀國，當身任利害，豈得遠怨市恩為自全計。

translations.literal: He once said: "When great ministers plan for the state, they should personally bear benefit and harm—how can they keep distant resentment and trade favors as a plan for self-preservation?"
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "When great ministers serve the state, they must shoulder its gains and losses themselves. How can they court distant favor and trade in kindness merely to save themselves?"

sentences.zh: 」故榆林始事，怨讟叢起，子俊持之益堅，竟以成功，為數世利。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Yulin project began, complaints and slander gathered, yet Zijun held firmer, and in the end succeeded, bringing benefit for many generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when work at Yulin began, complaints and slander piled up, yet Zijun held all the firmer and in the end prevailed, to the lasting benefit of many generations.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，居母憂時，令子寘毋會試，曰：「雖無律令，吾心不忍也。

translations.literal: He was filial and friendly by nature; during mourning for his mother he ordered his son Zhi not to take the metropolitan examination, saying: "Though there is no statute, my heart cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and devoted to his kin; while mourning his mother he forbade his son Zhi to sit for the metropolitan examination, saying, "There may be no law against it, but my heart will not allow it."

sentences.zh: 」嘗蔭子，移以蔭弟。

translations.literal: He once used hereditary privilege for his son but transferred it to privilege his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he was entitled to extend hereditary privilege to his son, but transferred the benefit to his younger brother instead.

sentences.zh: 子寰，舉進士，終戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Huan passed the jinshi and ended as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan passed the jinshi examination and rose to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 寘，就武蔭為錦衣千戶，終指揮同知。

translations.literal: Zhi took military hereditary privilege and became a thousand-household in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, ending as Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi entered service through military hereditary privilege as a thousand-household in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and ended his career as Assistant Commander.

sentences.zh: 曾孫承勛、承業，皆進士。

translations.literal: Great-grandsons Chengxun and Chengye were both jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandsons Chengxun and Chengye both became jinshi.

sentences.zh: 承勛，翰林修撰。

translations.literal: Chengxun was a Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun served as a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 承業，雲南僉事。

translations.literal: Chengye was a surveillance vice commissioner in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye served as Surveillance Vice Commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 阮勤，本交阯人，其父內徙，占籍長子。

translations.literal: Ruan Qin was originally from Jiaozhi; his father moved inward and registered domicile in Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Qin was originally from Jiaozhi; his father resettled inland and established household registration in Changzi.

sentences.zh: 勤舉景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: Qin passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Qin passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 歷臺州知府。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 清慎有惠政，賜誥旌異。

translations.literal: Scrupulous and cautious with benevolent administration, he was granted an edict of commendation for outstanding service.
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous in conduct and careful in office, his benevolent rule earned him an edict of special commendation.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he was grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he served as Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 築墩臺十四所，治垣塹三十餘里。

translations.literal: He built fourteen tower-forts and repaired more than thirty li of wall and ditch.
translations.idiomatic: He built fourteen beacon-tower forts and repaired more than thirty li of wall and ditch.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏免七府租四十余萬石。

translations.literal: In a famine year he memorialized exemption of seven prefectures' rent of more than four hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he memorialized to remit more than four hundred thousand shi of grain rent across seven prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入為侍郎，調南京刑部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice minister and was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a vice minister and then transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 蠻邦人著聲中國者，勤為最。

translations.literal: Among those from barbarian lands who made a name in China, Qin was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among men from the southern borderlands who won renown at the Ming court, none stood higher than Qin.

sentences.zh: 朱英，字時傑，桂陽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Ying, styled Shijie, was a man of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ying, whose courtesy name was Shijie, came from Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 五歲而孤。

translations.literal: He was orphaned at five.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of five.

sentences.zh: 力學，舉正統十年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: He studied diligently, passed the jinshi in the tenth year of Zhengtong, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with great diligence, passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign, and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 浙、閩盜起，簡御史十三人與中官分守諸府，英守處州。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Zhe and Min, thirteen censors were selected to divide with eunuchs in guarding the prefectures; Ying guarded Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry erupted in Zhejiang and Fujian, thirteen censors were chosen to pair with eunuchs in defending the prefectures; Ying was assigned to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 而葉宗留黨四出剽掠，處州道梗。

translations.literal: But Ye Zongliu's faction ranged out on all sides plundering, and the road to Chuzhou was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zongliu's followers, however, were raiding on every side, and the route to Chuzhou was cut off.

sentences.zh: 英間道馳至，撫降甚眾，戮賊首周明松等，賊散去乃還。

translations.literal: Ying went by a hidden road at full gallop, pacified and accepted surrender of very many, executed the bandit chiefs Zhou Mingsong and others, and the bandits scattered and left before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ying took a back road at full gallop, won over a great many through persuasion and surrender, executed the bandit leaders Zhou Mingsong and others, and only after the raiders had dispersed did he return.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，御史王豪嘗以勘陳循爭地事，忤循，為所訐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, Censor Wang Hao had once, in investigating Chen Xun's land dispute, offended Xun and was impeached by him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign, Censor Wang Hao had investigated a land dispute involving Chen Xun, offended him, and been impeached by Xun.

sentences.zh: 至是，循草詔，言風憲官被訐者，雖經赦宥，悉與外除。

translations.literal: At this point Xun drafted an edict saying that surveillance officials who had been impeached, even if pardoned by amnesty, should all be transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xun drafted an edict stating that any surveillance official who had been impeached, even if later pardoned by amnesty, must be transferred out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 於是豪當改知縣，英言：「若如詔書，則凡遭御史抨擊之人，皆將挾仇誣訐，而御史愈緘默不言矣。

translations.literal: Thus Hao was to be changed to magistrate; Ying said: "If according to the edict, then all who have been struck by censors will hold grudges and lodge false impeachments, and censors will grow ever more silent."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao was therefore to be demoted to magistrate; Ying protested, "If the edict stands, anyone who has ever crossed a censor will nurse a grudge and lodge false charges, and censors will only grow more afraid to speak."

sentences.zh: 」章下法司，請如英言，乃復豪職。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the law office; they requested as Ying said, and Hao's post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of Justice, which recommended accepting Ying's view, and Hao's post was restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為廣東右參議。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Right Assistant Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Assistant Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 過家省母，橐中惟賜金十兩。

translations.literal: Passing home to visit his mother, in his bag there was only ten taels of bestowed gold.
translations.idiomatic: On his way home to visit his mother, he carried only ten taels of gold the court had bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 抵任，撫雕瘵流亡。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he comforted the wasted and destitute refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office he comforted the destitute and those displaced by hardship.

sentences.zh: 立均徭法，十歲一更，民稱便。

translations.literal: He established an equal corvée law, renewed every ten years; the people praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted a system of equalized corvée labor, reassessed every ten years, and the people welcomed the reform.

sentences.zh: 天順初，兩廣賊愈熾，諸將多濫殺冒功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, bandits in the two Guangs grew fiercer; the generals mostly killed indiscriminately to claim merit falsely.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign banditry in the two Guangs grew worse, and many generals slaughtered indiscriminately to inflate their battle honors.

sentences.zh: 巡撫葉盛屬英督察。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng entrusted Ying to supervise and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng put Ying in charge of oversight.

sentences.zh: 參將範信誣宋泰、永平二鄉民為賊，屠戮殆盡，又欲屠進城鄉。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Fan Xin falsely accused the people of Songtai and Yongping townships as bandits, slaughtering nearly all, and also wished to slaughter Jincheng township.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Fan Xin falsely denounced the people of Songtai and Yongping as rebels and slaughtered nearly all of them; he then planned to do the same to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 英馳訊，悉縱去。

translations.literal: Ying rode in haste to investigate and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ying rode at once to investigate and ordered every captive released.

sentences.zh: 信忿，留師不還。

translations.literal: Xin was resentful and kept his army from returning.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xin was furious and refused to withdraw his troops.

sentences.zh: 英密請於盛，檄信班師，一方始靖。

translations.literal: Ying secretly requested of Sheng and issued an order recalling Xin; the region was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ying secretly appealed to Sheng, who issued orders recalling Fan Xin; only then was the region pacified.

sentences.zh: 潮州賊羅劉寧等流劫遠近，屢挫官兵。

translations.literal: Chaozhou bandits Luo, Liu, Ning, and others raided far and near, repeatedly defeating government troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Chaozhou, the bandits Luo, Liu, Ning, and their followers plundered far and wide and repeatedly routed the government forces.

sentences.zh: 英會師破滅之。

translations.literal: Ying combined armies and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ying mustered a joint force and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 還所掠人口數千，別置一營以處婦女，人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: He returned several thousand people they had seized; he separately set up one camp to house women, and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: He restored several thousand captives to their homes, set apart a separate camp for the women, and no soldier dared molest them.

sentences.zh: 官參議十年，進右參政。

translations.literal: In office as vice commissioner ten years, he was advanced to right vice grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years as a vice commissioner, he was promoted to right vice grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 成化初服闋，補陜西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, when mourning ended, he was assigned to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua reign began and his mourning period ended, he was posted to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 大軍討滿四，英主饋餉有功。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Man Si, Ying took charge of provisions and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the great expedition against Man Si, Ying directed the supply lines and earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 歷福建、陜西左、右布政使，皆推行均徭法。

translations.literal: He successively served as left and right provincial administration commissioners of Fujian and Shaanxi, all implementing the equal corvée law.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right administration commissioner in Fujian and Shaanxi, and in each post extended the equalized corvée system.

sentences.zh: 十年以右副都御史巡撫甘肅，先後陳安邊二十八事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made right assistant censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Gansu, and successively presented twenty-eight items on securing the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu, where he submitted twenty-eight proposals for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其請徙居戎、安流離、簡貢使，於時務尤切。

translations.literal: His requests to relocate the Rong, settle An's displaced, and simplify tribute envoys were especially urgent in the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: His proposals to relocate frontier Rong communities, resettle An's displaced subjects, and streamline tribute missions were especially pressing affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，兩廣總督吳琛卒，廷議以英前在廣東有威信，遂以代琛。

translations.literal: The next year in winter, Grand Coordinator of the Two Guangs Wu Chen died; court discussion held that because Ying had earlier authority in Guangdong, he was appointed to replace Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Wu Chen, Grand Coordinator of the Two Guangs, died. The court decided that Ying's earlier standing in Guangdong made him the right man to succeed Chen.

sentences.zh: 自韓雍大征以來，將帥喜邀功，利俘掠，名為「雕剿」。

translations.literal: Since Han Yong's great campaigns, generals liked to invite merit and profit from captive plunder, called "diaojiao."
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Yong's major campaigns, commanders had grown fond of inflating their battle honors and profiting from captives and plunder in what they called "hawk-strike" sweeps.

sentences.zh: 英至，鎮以寧靜，約飭將士。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived, he pacified with tranquility and admonished the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying took office he restored calm and issued strict orders to his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 毋得張賊聲勢，妄請用師。

translations.literal: They must not exaggerate bandit strength and recklessly request troops.
translations.idiomatic: They were forbidden to exaggerate rebel strength or recklessly demand additional troops.

sentences.zh: 招撫瑤、僮效順者，定為編戶，給復三年。

translations.literal: Those Yao and Zhuang who submitted through pacification were fixed as registered households and given tax relief for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zhuang who came in peacefully were registered as regular households and granted three years' tax relief.

sentences.zh: 於是馬平、陽朔、蒼梧諸縣蠻悉望風附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribes of Maping, Yangshuo, Cangwu, and other counties all attached at the wind's rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribal peoples of Maping, Yangshuo, Cangwu, and neighboring counties submitted in waves.

sentences.zh: 而荔波賊李公主有眾數萬，久負固，亦遣子納款。

translations.literal: But the Libo bandit Li Gongzhu had a host of tens of thousands; long stubborn, he also sent his son to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Even Li Gongzhu of Libo, who commanded tens of thousands and had long held out, sent his son to tender submission.

sentences.zh: 為置永安州處之，俾其子孫世吏目。

translations.literal: He established Yong'an Prefecture to settle them and caused their descendants to serve as clerks in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Ying created Yong'an Prefecture to resettle them and arranged for their descendants to hold hereditary clerkships.

sentences.zh: 自是歸附日眾，凡為戶四萬三千有奇，口十五萬有奇。

translations.literal: From this, submission daily increased; altogether households forty-three thousand odd, mouths one hundred fifty thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Submissions then multiplied daily until the registered households exceeded forty-three thousand and the population more than one hundred fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官與督撫、總兵官坐次，中官居中，總督居總兵官左。

translations.literal: Seating order of garrison eunuchs with supervisors and grand coordinators and regional commanders: the eunuch in the center, the grand coordinator to the left of the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: At formal seating, the garrison eunuch sat in the center, with the grand coordinator to the regional commander's left.

sentences.zh: 時總兵官陳政以伯爵欲抑英居右，英不可，奏乞裁定。

translations.literal: At the time Regional Commander Chen Zheng, as an earl, wished to press Ying to the right; Ying would not accept it and memorialized begging adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Chen Zheng, holding an earldom, tried to seat Ying on his right; Ying refused and asked the throne to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 命解英總督，止為巡撫，居政下。

translations.literal: An order removed Ying's grand coordinator post; he was only grand supervisor, placed below Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped Ying of the grand coordinator title, leaving him only as grand supervisor and ranking him below Zheng.

sentences.zh: 尚書余子俊言英招徠功多，當增秩褒賞，乃反削其事權，恐無以鎮諸蠻。

translations.literal: Minister Yu Zijun said Ying's pacification and recruitment merit was great and he should receive higher rank and reward; yet instead they cut his authority—fearing he would be unable to pacify the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun argued that Ying's success in winning people over deserved promotion and reward, and that stripping his authority would leave him powerless to hold the tribes in check.

sentences.zh: 乃擢英右都御史仍總督，位次如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ying was promoted to right censor-in-chief and still grand coordinator; seating order as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was therefore promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief while retaining the grand coordinator post, with his precedence restored.

sentences.zh: 田州酋黃明烝其知府岑溥祖母，欲殺溥。

translations.literal: The Tianzhou chieftain Huang Ming violated the prefect Cen Pu's grandmother and wished to kill Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ming, a Tianzhou chieftain, assaulted Prefect Cen Pu's grandmother and plotted Pu's death.

sentences.zh: 溥出走思恩，明因肆屠戮。

translations.literal: Pu fled to Si'en; Ming therefore wantonly slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Pu fled to Si'en, whereupon Ming carried out a wholesale massacre.

sentences.zh: 英將進討，檄溥族人恩城知州岑欽殺明雪恥。

translations.literal: Ying was about to advance in attack and ordered Pu's clansman, Encheng Prefect Cen Qin, to kill Ming and avenge the shame.
translations.idiomatic: As Ying prepared to march, he ordered Cen Qin, prefect of Encheng and a kinsman of Pu, to kill Huang Ming and restore the family's honor.

sentences.zh: 欽遂誅明並其族屬，傳首軍門。

translations.literal: Qin then executed Ming and his clansmen and sent the head to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qin duly executed Ming and his kin and delivered the head to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 英淳厚，然持法無所假借。

translations.literal: Ying was honest and generous, yet in holding the law he made no allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was mild and upright by nature, yet utterly unyielding once the law was engaged.

sentences.zh: 與市舶中官韋眷忤，眷摭奏英專權玩賊。

translations.literal: He clashed with the maritime-trade eunuch Wei Juan; Juan gathered accusations and memorialized that Ying monopolized power and toyed with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Wei Juan, the maritime-trade eunuch, who manufactured charges that Ying abused his authority and coddled the rebels.

sentences.zh: 潯州知府史芳以事見責，亦訐英奸貪欺罔。

translations.literal: Xunzhou Prefect Shi Fang, because of matters, was reprimanded and also impeached Ying as treacherous, greedy, and deceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fang, prefect of Xunzhou, having been disciplined over another matter, joined in accusing Ying of corruption and deceit.

sentences.zh: 按皆無驗，乃鐫芳二官，諭眷協和共事。

translations.literal: Investigation found nothing verified; then Fang was degraded two ranks and Juan was instructed to cooperate in shared affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiries cleared Ying on every count; Fang was demoted two ranks and Juan was ordered to work with him in good faith.

sentences.zh: 十六年，交阯攻老撾，議者恐其內寇，詔問英處置之宜。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Jiaozhi attacked Laos; discussants feared they would invade inward, and an imperial order asked Ying how to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Jiaozhi attacked Laos. Fearing an incursion into the empire, the court asked Ying how the situation should be handled.

sentences.zh: 英對言：「彼不過爭甌脫耳，諭之當自悔懼。

translations.literal: Ying replied, saying: "They are merely contending over border pasturelands; admonish them and they should themselves repent and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Ying answered, "They are only quarreling over grazing rights on the frontier. A stern warning should bring them to repent and stand down."

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，果上表謝。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his words; indeed they submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice, and the Annamese soon sent a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 潯、梧、高、廉賊起，偕政等分道擊之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Xun, Wu, Gao, and Lian; together with Zheng and others they attacked by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose in Xun, Wuzhou, Gaozhou, and Lianzhou; Ying and Zheng divided their forces and struck on several fronts.

sentences.zh: 再戰，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In a second battle, captured and beheaded very many.
translations.idiomatic: After a second engagement they took and slew a great number.

sentences.zh: 十九年，桂林平樂蠻攻城殺將，英、政復分兵十二道擊破之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Pingyue tribes of Guilin attacked cities and killed generals; Ying and Zheng again divided troops in twelve paths and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Pingyue tribes of Guilin stormed towns and killed officers; Ying and Zheng once more routed them with twelve columns.

sentences.zh: 明年入掌都察院事，尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: The next year he entered to manage Censorate affairs and soon was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took charge of the Censorate and was soon named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 又明年正月，星變，疏陳八事：請禁邊將節旦獻馬；

translations.literal: Again the next year, first month, the stars changed; he memorialized presenting eight items: request to forbid border generals from presenting horses on festivals;
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, in the first month, an irregularity appeared in the heavens and he submitted eight reforms: he urged an end to border generals' holiday gifts of horses;

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官、武將不得私立莊田，侵奪官地；

translations.literal: garrison eunuchs and military officers must not privately establish manor fields or seize official lands;
translations.idiomatic: that garrison eunuchs and officers be barred from founding private estates or seizing government land;

sentences.zh: 燒丹符咒左道之人，當置重典；

translations.literal: those who burn elixirs, talismans, and left-path arts should face heavy statutes;
translations.idiomatic: that alchemists, sorcerers, and other practitioners of heterodox arts face severe punishment;

sentences.zh: 四方分守監槍內官勿進貢品物；

translations.literal: the four directions' garrison supervising gunner eunuchs must not advance tribute goods;
translations.idiomatic: that regional gunnery eunuchs cease sending tribute goods to court;

sentences.zh: 罷撤倉場、馬房、上林苑增設內侍；

translations.literal: abolish and withdraw warehouse yards, horse stalls, and Imperial Park posts that added inner attendants;
translations.idiomatic: that superfluous eunuchs attached to granaries, stables, and the Imperial Park be removed;

sentences.zh: 召還建言得罪諸臣；

translations.literal: recall the various ministers who offered remonstrance and suffered punishment;
translations.idiomatic: that officials punished for forthright remonstrance be recalled;

sentences.zh: 清內府收白糧積弊；

translations.literal: clear the inner treasury's collection of white-grain accumulated abuses;
translations.idiomatic: that abuses in the palace grain levy be rectified;

sentences.zh: 治奸民投獻莊田及貴戚受獻者罪。

translations.literal: punish wicked commoners who offered-up manor lands and noble relatives who received such offers.
translations.idiomatic: and that both the commoners who "donated" estates to the powerful and the nobles who accepted them be punished.

sentences.zh: 權幸皆不便，執政多持之不行。

translations.literal: Power favorites were all inconvenienced; those in power mostly held the proposals and did not implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals offended every vested interest at court, and the ministers in power mostly shelved them.

sentences.zh: 英造內閣力爭，竟不能盡從也。

translations.literal: Ying went to the Grand Secretariat to forcefully contend; in the end they could not entirely be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pressed his case before the Grand Secretariat, yet in the end most of his program went unenforced.

sentences.zh: 時流民集京師者多，英請人給米月三斗，幼者半之，報許。

translations.literal: At the time vagabonds gathered in the capital in great numbers; Ying requested that each person be given three dou of rice per month, half for the young; the reply permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: With refugees crowding the capital, he asked that each adult receive three dou of grain a month and each child half that amount; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 其年秋卒。

translations.literal: That year in autumn he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Junior Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 英為總督承韓雍、吳琛後。

translations.literal: Ying as grand coordinator succeeded after Han Yong and Wu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator, Ying followed in the footsteps of Han Yong and Wu Chen.

sentences.zh: 雍雖有大功，恢廓自奉，贈遺過侈，有司困供億，公私耗竭；

translations.literal: Yong though had great merit was expansive and self-indulgent; gifts were excessively lavish—local officials were strained by supplies, and public and private resources were exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Yong's campaigns had been magnificent, but he lived on a grand scale and his lavish gift-giving drained both the treasury and the provinces that had to supply him;

sentences.zh: 而琛務謹廉；

translations.literal: while Chen was devoted to careful frugality;
translations.idiomatic: Chen, by contrast, was scrupulously frugal;

sentences.zh: 至英益持清節，僅攜一蒼頭之官。

translations.literal: to Ying he further held pure integrity, going to office with only one gray-haired servant.
translations.idiomatic: and Ying surpassed them both in austerity, arriving at his posts attended by a single aged retainer.

sentences.zh: 先後屢賜璽書、金幣，英藏璽書，貯金幣於庫。

translations.literal: Successively and repeatedly bestowed imperial edicts and gold and coins; Ying stored the edicts and deposited the gold and coins in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts and gifts of gold were bestowed upon him again and again; he filed away the edicts and locked the gold in the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 其威望不及雍，而惠澤過之。

translations.literal: His prestige did not reach Yong's, yet his gracious blessings surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He never matched Yong's renown, yet the people benefited from his rule far more.

sentences.zh: 在甘肅積軍儲三十萬兩，廣四十余萬，皆不以聞。

translations.literal: In Gansu he accumulated army stores of three hundred thousand taels; in Guangdong more than four hundred thousand—all without reporting.
translations.idiomatic: In Gansu he built up three hundred thousand taels of military reserves, and in Guangdong more than four hundred thousand, yet he never mentioned either sum at court.

sentences.zh: 或問之，答曰：「此邊臣常分，何足言。

translations.literal: Some asked him; he answered: "This is a border officer's regular duty; what is worth mentioning?"
translations.idiomatic: When questioned, he said only, "Stockpiling supplies is what a frontier official is supposed to do—why make a fuss?"

sentences.zh: 」人服其知大體。

translations.literal: People admired his knowing the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it admired his sense of proportion.

sentences.zh: 正德中，追謚恭簡。

translations.literal: In Zhengde times, posthumously titled Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengde reign he was posthumously given the temple name Gongjian, "Respectful and Simple."

sentences.zh: 子守孚，進士，刑部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Shoufu, a jinshi, served as a bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoufu, also a jinshi, rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 秦纮，字世纓，單人。

translations.literal: Qin Hong, courtesy name Shiying, was a man of Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hong, whose courtesy name was Shiying, came from Shan County.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京御史。

translations.literal: Appointed Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劾治內官傅鎖兒罪，諫止江南采翠毛、魚魫等使。

translations.literal: He impeached and punished the inner attendant Fu Suo'er; he remonstrated to stop the Jiangnan envoys for kingfisher feathers and fish maw.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted the eunuch Fu Suo'er and remonstrated against the Jiangnan missions sent to collect kingfisher feathers and fish maw.

sentences.zh: 權貴忌之，蜚語聞。

translations.literal: The powerful and noble resented him; slanderous words reached [the throne].
translations.idiomatic: The powerful took offense, and calumny reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 會考察，坐謫湖廣驛丞。

translations.literal: When the evaluation occurred, he was sentenced to demotion to Huguang relay-station assistant.
translations.idiomatic: At the next personnel review he was demoted to assistant at a Huguang courier station.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年擢右僉都御史，巡撫山西，奏鎮國將軍奇澗等罪。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi, and memorialized the crimes of State-Stabilizing General Qi Run and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shanxi, where he impeached State-Stabilizing General Qi Run and others.

sentences.zh: 奇澗父慶成王鐘鎰為奏辯，且誣纮。

translations.literal: Qi Run's father, Prince Qingcheng Zhong Yi, memorialized in defense and also slandered Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Run's father, Prince Qingcheng Zhong Yi, petitioned in his son's defense and slandered Hong in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝重違王意，逮纮下法司治。

translations.literal: The Emperor heavily weighed against the prince's wish, arrested Hong, and sent him to the judiciary for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to offend the prince, the emperor had Hong arrested and handed over to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 事皆無驗，而內官尚亨籍纮家，以所得敝衣數事奏。

translations.literal: The matters were all unverified, yet the inner attendant Shang Heng searched Hong's house and memorialized with several tattered garments obtained.
translations.idiomatic: None of the charges held, but the eunuch Shang Heng searched Hong's home and reported back with nothing but a few threadbare garments.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「纮貧一至此耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed, saying: "Is Hong's poverty to this extent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Can Hong really be this poor?"

sentences.zh: 」賜鈔萬貫旌之。

translations.literal: He bestowed ten thousand strings of paper money to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with ten thousand strings of paper money in recognition of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 於是奪奇澗等三人爵，王亦削祿三之一，而改纮撫河南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi Run and three others had their ranks seized; the prince also had his stipend reduced by one-third; and Hong was transferred to grand coordinate Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Run and three others were stripped of their titles, the prince's stipend was cut by a third, and Hong was reassigned to Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋復調宣府。

translations.literal: Soon he was again transferred to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred again to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 小王子數萬騎寇大同，長驅入順聖川，掠宣府境。

translations.literal: The Little Prince with tens of thousands of horsemen raided Datong, long drove into Shunsheng River valley, and plundered Xuanfu territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince led tens of thousands of horsemen against Datong, swept deep into the Shunsheng River valley, and raided the Xuanfu frontier.

sentences.zh: 纮與總兵官周玉等邀擊，遁去。

translations.literal: Hong with Regional Commander Zhou Yu and others intercepted and struck; they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Regional Commander Zhou Yu intercepted the raiders and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 尋入掠興寧口，連戰卻之，追還所掠，璽書勞焉。

translations.literal: Soon they entered again to plunder Xingning Pass; repeatedly battling they repelled them, pursued and recovered what had been seized; an imperial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When they struck again at Xingning Pass he beat them back in successive engagements, recovered the booty, and received an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 進左僉都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief; grand coordinator as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief while retaining the grand coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召還理院事，遷戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to manage court affairs and moved to right vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled to the capital to handle Censorate business and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 萬安逐尹旻，誣纮旻黨，降廣西右參政。

translations.literal: Wan An expelled Yin Min and slandered Hong as Min's faction; he was demoted to right participating grand secretary of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan An drove out Yin Min he smeared Hong as one of Min's partisans and had him demoted to Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 進福建左布政使。

translations.literal: Advanced to left provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Left Administration Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年以王恕薦，擢左副都御史，督漕運。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, on Wang Shu's recommendation, he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and supervised grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi, on Wang Shu's recommendation, he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Superintendent of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 明年三月進右都御史，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: The next year, third month, he was advanced to right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of the military affairs of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: The following third month he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and placed in overall command of military affairs in the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「中官、武將總鎮兩廣者，率縱私人擾商賈，高居私家。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Eunuchs and military officers who chiefly guard the Two Guangs mostly indulge private persons to harass merchants and dwell loftily in private homes.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The eunuchs and generals who hold supreme command in the Two Guangs routinely let their retainers harass merchants while they themselves live in private mansions.

sentences.zh: 擅理公事，賊殺不辜，交通土官為奸利。

translations.literal: They usurp handling of public affairs, kill the innocent, and communicate with native officials for wicked profit.
translations.idiomatic: They seize civil authority, murder without cause, and collude with tribal officials for illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 而天下鎮守官皆得擅執軍職，受民訟，非制，請嚴禁絕。

translations.literal: Yet throughout the realm garrison officials may usurp military duties and receive people's lawsuits—against regulation; I request strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, garrison commissioners everywhere have taken it upon themselves to command troops and hear civil suits, which is contrary to statute; I ask that this be forbidden outright.

sentences.zh: 總鎮府故有賞功所，歲儲金錢數萬，費出無經，宜從都御史勾稽。

translations.literal: The supreme commander's office formerly had a rewards office, yearly storing gold and money in the tens of thousands; expenditures had no regularity—it should be audited by the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's headquarters maintains a reward fund of tens of thousands of taels each year with no proper accounting; it should be placed under the censor-in-chief's oversight.

sentences.zh: 廣、潮、南、韶多盜，當設社學，編保甲，以絕盜源。

translations.literal: Guang, Chao, Nan, and Shao have many bandits; community schools should be established and baojia organized to cut off the source of banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou, Chaozhou, Nan'ao, and Shaoguan are rife with bandits; local schools and baojia militia should be established to dry up the roots of disorder."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor entirely followed his requests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 恩城知州岑欽攻逐田州知府岑溥，與泗城知州岑應分據其地。

translations.literal: Encheng Prefect Cen Qin attacked and drove out Tianzhou Prefect Cen Pu; with Sicheng Prefect Cen Ying he divided and occupied his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Qin, prefect of Encheng, attacked and expelled Cen Pu, prefect of Tianzhou, and together with Cen Ying of Sicheng carved up Pu's domain.

sentences.zh: 纮入田州逐走欽，還溥於府，留官軍戍之，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Hong entered Tianzhou, drove away Qin, returned Pu to the prefecture, left official troops to garrison it, and the disorder was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong marched into Tianzhou, expelled Qin, restored Pu to office, and left government troops to garrison the region until order returned.

sentences.zh: 復遣將討平黎賊陵水，瑤賊德慶。

translations.literal: He again sent generals to attack and pacify the Li bandits of Lingshui and the Yao bandits of Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched generals to suppress the Li rebels of Lingshui and the Yao rebels of Deqing.

sentences.zh: 纮之初蒞鎮也，劾總兵官安遠侯柳景貪暴，逮下獄。

translations.literal: When Hong first arrived to take command, he impeached Regional Commander Marquis of Anyuan Liu Jing for greed and cruelty and arrested and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after taking command he impeached Liu Jing, the Marquis of Anyuan and regional commander, for rapacity and cruelty and had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 景亦訐纮，勘無左證，法司當景死。

translations.literal: Jing also impeached Hong; investigation found no supporting evidence; the judiciary sentenced Jing to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jing counter-attacked with charges of his own, but the inquiry turned up nothing against Hong while the judiciary ruled that Jing deserved death.

sentences.zh: 景連姻周太后家，有奧援，訐纮不已。

translations.literal: Jing had marriage ties with Empress Dowager Zhou's family and had hidden support; he impeached Hong without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was related by marriage to the Zhou empress dowager's clan and enjoyed powerful backing, and he kept accusing Hong.

sentences.zh: 詔並逮纮，廷鞫卒無罪。

translations.literal: An imperial order arrested both; court trial in the end found no guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered both men brought to the capital for trial; in the end Hong was cleared of every charge.

sentences.zh: 詔宥景死，奪爵閑住，而纮亦罷歸。

translations.literal: An imperial order pardoned Jing from death, stripped his title and confined him to idle residence, while Hong was also dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The throne pardoned Jing from the death sentence, stripped him of his title, and confined him to private life, while Hong too was removed from office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 大臣王恕等請留纮，不納。

translations.literal: Senior ministers Wang Shu and others requested to retain Hong; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu and other senior ministers pleaded that Hong be kept in office, but the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 廷臣復連章言纮可大用。

translations.literal: Court ministers again submitted linked memorials saying Hong could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials again submitted memorial after memorial urging that Hong be given a post commensurate with his talents.

sentences.zh: 居數月，起南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After several months, he was summoned as Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was recalled to serve as Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十一年引疾去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he cited illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，寇大入花馬池，敗官軍孔壩溝，直抵平涼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, bandits entered Huamachi in force, defeated the official army at Kongba Ditch, and drove straight to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year the raiders poured into Huamachi, routed government troops at Kongba Ditch, and pressed on to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 言者謂纮有威名，雖老可用。

translations.literal: Speakers said Hong had a reputation for awe-inspiring authority; though old, he could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that Hong's name alone still inspired fear and that, despite his age, he remained fit for service.

sentences.zh: 詔起戶部尚書兼右副都御史，總制三邊軍務。

translations.literal: An order summoned him as Minister of Revenue concurrently with Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supervising military affairs on the Three Frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief with overall command of military affairs on the Three Frontiers.

sentences.zh: 纮馳至固原，按行敗所。

translations.literal: Hong galloped to Guyuan and inspected on foot the place of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Hong rode posthaste to Guyuan and personally surveyed the scene of the rout.

sentences.zh: 躬祭陣亡將士，掩其骼。

translations.literal: He personally sacrificed to the fallen officers and soldiers and buried their bones.
translations.idiomatic: He offered sacrifice himself to the men who had died in battle and saw their remains laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 奏錄死事指揮朱鼎等五人，恤軍士戰歿者家。

translations.literal: He memorialized to register five who died in service, including Commander Zhu Ding, and to relieve the families of soldiers killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Zhu Ding and four other commanders who had died in action be entered in the rolls of honor, and that the families of soldiers killed in battle receive relief.

sentences.zh: 劾治敗將楊琳等四人罪，更易守將。

translations.literal: He impeached and punished the crimes of four defeated generals including Yang Lin and replaced the garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Yang Lin and three other defeated commanders, had them punished, and replaced the frontier garrison leaders.

sentences.zh: 練壯士，興屯田，申明號令，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: He drilled stalwart men, promoted military colonies, clarified orders and prohibitions, and the army's reputation greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled picked troops, expanded military colonies, and enforced discipline until the army's morale and reputation soared anew.

sentences.zh: 初，寇未入河套，平涼、固原皆內地，無患。

translations.literal: At first, before bandits entered the Ordos loop, Pingliang and Guyuan were both interior territory and free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times, before the raiders pushed into the Ordos, Pingliang and Guyuan had lain deep inside the empire and knew no threat.

sentences.zh: 自孛來往牧後，固原當兵沖，為平、慶、臨、鞏門戶。

translations.literal: After Bolai came to pasture there, Guyuan bore the brunt of military pressure and became the gateway for Ping, Qing, Lin, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bolai had moved his herds into the region, Guyuan stood in the path of every campaign and became the gate guarding Pingliang, Qingyang, Lintao, and Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 而城隘民貧，兵力單弱，商販不至。

translations.literal: Yet the city was cramped, the people poor, military strength meager and weak, and merchants and peddlers did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the city was cramped, the people impoverished, the garrison thin, and merchants would not venture near.

sentences.zh: 纮乃拓治城郭，招徠商賈，建改為州，而身留節制之。

translations.literal: Hong then expanded and repaired the walls and moats, attracted merchants, memorialized to change it to a prefecture, and himself remained to command and restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong widened and strengthened the fortifications, drew traders back, petitioned to elevate the district to a prefecture, and stayed on himself as its military commander.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「固原主、客兵止萬八千人，散守城堡二十四。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Guyuan's main and auxiliary troops number only eighteen thousand, scattered guarding twenty-four forts and castles.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating, "Guyuan has only eighteen thousand regular and auxiliary troops, spread across twenty-four forts.

sentences.zh: 勢分力弱，宜益兵。

translations.literal: Strength is divided and force weak; troops should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Their strength is divided and too thin on the ground; the garrison should be reinforced.

sentences.zh: 舊臨、鞏、秦州諸軍歲赴甘、涼備禦。

translations.literal: Formerly the armies of Lin, Gong, and Qinzhou yearly went to Gan and Liang for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the forces of Lintao, Gongchang, and Qinzhou have been sent to Ganzhou and Liangzhou for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 及他方有警，又調兵甘、涼，或發京軍征討。

translations.literal: When elsewhere there was an alarm, troops were again transferred from Gan and Liang, or capital troops were dispatched for punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever trouble flares elsewhere, men are stripped from Ganzhou and Liangzhou, or the capital sends out its own expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 夫京師天下本，邊將手握重兵，而一遇有事輒請京軍，非強幹弱枝之道。

translations.literal: Now the capital is the root of the realm; border generals hold heavy troops in their hands, yet at the first sign of trouble they immediately request capital troops—this is not the way of a strong trunk and weak branches.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the root of the empire, and frontier commanders already hold substantial forces—yet at the first alarm they clamor for troops from Beijing. That is not how one keeps a strong center and capable periphery.

sentences.zh: 請自今京兵毋輕發，臨、鞏、甘、涼諸軍亦宜各還本鎮。

translations.literal: I request that from now capital troops not be lightly dispatched, and that the armies of Lin, Gong, Gan, and Liang also each return to their home garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the capital armies should not be committed lightly, and the troops of Lintao, Gongchang, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou should each return to their home posts.

sentences.zh: 但選知兵宿將一二人各守其地，人以戍為家，軍以將為命，自樂趨役，而有戰心，計之得者也。

translations.literal: Only select one or two veteran generals who know warfare to each guard their territory; let men take garrison duty as home, let the army take the general as its command—then they will gladly hasten to service and possess a will to fight. This is a plan that succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Choose one or two seasoned commanders who know war and let each hold his own ground. Let the men treat their garrison as home and the troops take their general as their fate; they will serve willingly and fight with heart. That, I believe, is the sound course."

sentences.zh: 」纮見固原迤北延袤千里，閑田數十萬頃，曠野近邊，無城堡可依。

translations.literal: Hong saw that north of Guyuan, winding along for a thousand li, there were hundreds of thousands of mu of idle land—open wilderness near the border with no forts or castles to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Hong observed that the country north of Guyuan stretched a thousand li with hundreds of thousands of mu of unused land—open steppe along the frontier with no fortifications to shelter it.

sentences.zh: 議於花馬池迤西至小鹽池二百里，每二十里築一堡，堡周四十八丈，役軍五百人。

translations.literal: He proposed that from Huamachi winding west to Xiaoyanchi for two hundred li, every twenty li a fort be built; each fort's perimeter forty-eight zhang, employing five hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that along the two hundred li from Huamachi west to Xiaoyanchi a fort be built every twenty li—each with a perimeter of forty-eight zhang and garrisoned by five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 固原迤北諸處亦各築屯堡，募人屯種，每頃歲賦米五石，可得五十萬石。

translations.literal: At various places north of Guyuan, winding along, he also built military colony forts each in its place, recruited people to farm colonies, and with five shi of grain levied per qing yearly, five hundred thousand shi could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Along the northern approaches to Guyuan he likewise built colony forts, recruited settlers to farm the land, and reckoned that at five shi of grain per qing in annual rent the yield could reach five hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 規畫已定，而寧夏巡撫劉憲為梗。

translations.literal: The planning was already settled, but Ningxia Grand Coordinator Liu Xian became an obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The plans were already settled when Liu Xian, grand coordinator of Ningxia, threw himself in the way.

sentences.zh: 纮乃奏曰：「竊見三邊情形，延綏、甘、涼地雖廣，而士馬精強。

translations.literal: Hong then memorialized, saying: "I have observed in private the situation on the Three Frontiers: though the lands of Yansui, Gan, and Liang are broad, their troops and horses are elite and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then submitted a memorial: "In my view the Three Frontiers present this picture: Yansui, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou cover vast ground, yet their troops and horses are seasoned and strong.

sentences.zh: 寧夏怯弱矣，然河山險阻。

translations.literal: Ningxia is timid and weak, yet its rivers and mountains are perilous and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia's forces are the weakest, but rivers and mountains make its terrain formidable.

sentences.zh: 惟花馬池至固原，軍既怯弱，又墩臺疏遠，敵騎得長驅深入，故當增築墩堡。

translations.literal: Only from Huamachi to Guyuan—the army is both timid and weak, and watchtowers and beacon platforms are sparse and far apart, so enemy cavalry can drive in deeply at a gallop; therefore forts and watchtowers should be increased and built.
