translations.idiomatic: Only the stretch from Huamachi to Guyuan combines weak troops with watchtowers spaced too far apart, allowing enemy horsemen to ride deep without check. That is where forts and beacon towers must be added.

sentences.zh: 韋州、豫望城諸處亦然。

translations.literal: Weizhou, Yuwangcheng, and various other places are likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: The same holds for Weizhou, Yuwangcheng, and the like.

sentences.zh: 今固原迤南修築將畢，惟花馬池迤北二百里當築十堡。

translations.literal: Now construction south of Guyuan, winding along, is nearly complete; only north of Huamachi, winding along, for two hundred li ten forts should be built.
translations.idiomatic: Work south of Guyuan is nearly finished; only the two hundred li north of Huamachi still requires ten forts.

sentences.zh: 而憲危言阻眾，且廢垂成之功。

translations.literal: Yet Xian's alarming words obstructed the multitude and moreover wasted work on the verge of completion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xian has sown alarm to block the project and would abandon work already within reach of completion.

sentences.zh: 乞令憲制三邊，而改臣撫寧夏，俾得終邊防，於事為便。

translations.literal: I beg that Xian be ordered to command the Three Frontiers, while I be changed to pacify Ningxia, so that I may finish the border defenses—this would be convenient for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xian be placed in overall command of the Three Frontiers while I am reassigned to pacify Ningxia, so that I may see the frontier works through to the end. That would serve the public interest best."

sentences.zh: 」帝下詔責憲，憲引罪，卒行纮策。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict reprimanding Xian; Xian confessed guilt, and in the end Hong's plan was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict rebuking Xian. Xian confessed his fault, and in the end Hong's plan went forward.

sentences.zh: 修築諸邊城堡一萬四千余所，垣塹六千四百餘里，固原屹為重鎮。

translations.literal: He built and repaired border forts and castles in excess of fourteen thousand places, ramparts and ditches in excess of six thousand four hundred li, and Guyuan stood firm as a great strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: More than fourteen thousand frontier forts and castles were built or repaired, with ramparts and ditches stretching over six thousand four hundred li, until Guyuan rose as a mighty bastion.

sentences.zh: 纮又以意作戰車，名「全勝車」，詔頒其式於諸邊。

translations.literal: Hong also according to his own conception made a war chariot, named the "Total Victory Chariot," and an imperial order promulgated its pattern to all frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also designed a war chariot of his own devising, which he called the "Chariot of Total Victory," and an edict distributed its specifications to every frontier command.

sentences.zh: 在事三年，四鎮晏然，前後經略西陲者莫及。

translations.literal: In office three years, the four garrisons were peaceful and secure; those who before and after strategized the western borderlands could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: During three years in command the four frontier districts knew peace, and none who had governed the western marches before or since could equal his achievement.

sentences.zh: 十七年加太子少保，召還視部事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and summoned back to oversee ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and recalled to the capital to resume his duties at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 以年老連章力辭，乞致仕。

translations.literal: Because of old age he submitted linked memorials vigorously declining and begged to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his advanced age, he memorialized again and again, pressing his refusal, and petitioned for retirement.

sentences.zh: 詔賜敕乘傳歸，月廩歲隸如制。

translations.literal: An order granted him an imperial letter and post-horse carriage to return home; monthly grain stipend and yearly retainers followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him an imperial letter of commendation and post-horses for the journey home, with monthly grain and annual retainers as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 明年九月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following ninth month, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Xiangyi, "Assisting and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 纮廉介絕俗，妻孥菜羹麥飯常不飽。

translations.literal: Hong's integrity and frugality were beyond the common run; his wife and children with vegetable broth and barley meal were often not full.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was incorruptible to a degree that set him apart from his age; his wife and children often went hungry on nothing but vegetable broth and barley gruel.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，勇於除害，不自顧慮，士大夫識與不識稱為偉人。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and resolute; he was brave in removing harm and did not consider himself—whether gentry knew him or not, they called him a great man.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and decisive by nature, he struck at wrongdoing without regard for his own safety, and men of letters, whether they knew him or not, hailed him as a towering figure.

sentences.zh: 在兩廣被逮時，方議討後山賊。

translations.literal: When he was arrested in the Two Guangs, they were just then deliberating on attacking the Back Mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When he was arrested in Guangdong and Guangxi, the command was still debating an expedition against the bandits of the Back Mountains.

sentences.zh: 治軍事畢，從容就道，儀衛騶從不貶損。

translations.literal: When military affairs were settled he finished them, then calmly took to the road; ceremonial guards and mounted attendants were not reduced or diminished.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the military business through to its end, then set out on the road at an unhurried pace, his full escort and retinue undiminished.

sentences.zh: 既逾嶺，始囚服就系。

translations.literal: Having already crossed the ridge, only then in prisoner's garb did he submit to binding.
translations.idiomatic: Only after he had crossed the mountains did he don prisoner's dress and submit to restraint.

sentences.zh: 謂官校曰：「兩廣蠻夷雜處，總制體尊，遽就拘執，損國威。

translations.literal: He said to the official guards: "The Two Guangs are a place where barbarians and Yi are mixed; the supreme commander's dignity is lofty—hastily submitting to arrest and binding damages the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: He told the escort officers, "Guangdong and Guangxi are lands where barbarians mingle with the settled population. A supreme commander's station is a lofty one; to seize him at once would diminish the empire's dignity.

sentences.zh: 今既逾嶺，真囚矣。

translations.literal: Now that I have already crossed the ridge, I am a true prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have crossed the mountains, I am in truth your prisoner."

sentences.zh: 」其嚴重得體如此。

translations.literal: His gravity and propriety were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the gravity and tact with which he bore himself.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，劉瑾亂政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde, Liu Jin threw the government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhengde reign Liu Jin threw the government into chaos.

sentences.zh: 纮家奴憾纮婦弟楊瑾，以纮所遺火炮投緝事校尉，誣瑾畜違禁軍器。

translations.literal: Hong's household slave resented Hong's wife's younger brother Yang Jin; he cast cannon Hong had bequeathed to the secret-service guards and falsely accused Jin of hoarding prohibited military weapons.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave of Hong's, bearing a grudge against Hong's brother-in-law Yang Jin, turned over to the secret police a cannon Hong had once given away and falsely accused Jin of stockpiling forbidden arms.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾怒，歸罪於纮。

translations.literal: Liu Jin was angry and laid the blame on Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin flew into a rage and turned the blame on Hong.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，無所得。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated and registered; nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: His property was confiscated, yet nothing of value was found.

sentences.zh: 言官張九敘、塗敬等復希瑾意劾纮，士類嗤之。

translations.literal: Censorial officials Zhang Jiuxu, Tu Jing, and others again catered to Jin's intent and impeached Hong; the scholar class mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Zhang Jiuxu, Tu Jing, and others again impeached Hong to curry favor with Jin, and men of learning held them in contempt.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：項忠、韓雍皆以文學通籍，而親提桴鼓，樹勛戎馬之場。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Xiang Zhong and Han Yong both entered the official register through literary studies, yet personally raised the war drum and planted merit on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Xiang Zhong and Han Yong both rose through the civil examinations, yet took up the war drum in person and won their laurels amid the clash of arms.

sentences.zh: 其應機決勝，成畫遠謀，雖宿將殆無以過，豈不壯哉！

translations.literal: Their responding to opportunity and deciding victory, completing designs and far-reaching stratagems—even veteran generals could hardly surpass them. Is it not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: In seizing the moment, carrying the day, and executing far-sighted designs, they outshone even seasoned commanders. What could be more splendid!

sentences.zh: 賞不酬勞，謠諑繼起，文法吏從而繩其後，功名之士所為發憤而太息也。

translations.literal: Rewards did not repay their labor; slanderous words arose in succession; legalist clerks followed and bound them afterward—what men of achievement and fame do in indignation, sighing deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet reward never matched their service; slander followed slander, and the pedants of the law courts came after to snare them. It is over such fates that men of merit clench their fists and sigh.

sentences.zh: 余子俊盡心邊計，數世賴之。

translations.literal: Yu Zijun exhausted his heart on frontier plans; several generations relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun gave his whole heart to frontier strategy, and generations reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 朱英廉威名粵嶠，秦纮經略著西陲，文武兼資，偉哉一代之能臣矣！

translations.literal: Zhu Ying's integrity and awe-inspiring authority made his name on the Guang peaks; Qin Hong's frontier strategy was renowned on the western borderlands—civil and martial both equipped. Magnificent are such able ministers of a generation!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ying won fame in Guangdong through integrity and stern authority; Qin Hong's frontier governance made him a legend on the western marches. Civil and martial talent in one man—what magnificent servants of the state a single age could produce!
